docs.title: Phase 0 — Close and preserve the current baseline
docs.text:
Status: completed on 2026-08-05. The latent-space metric-compatibility and inverse-PLS studies are archived, and their capability specifications are canonical.

Purpose: ensure the conclusions already reached remain reproducible and discoverable.

Work:

  • Archive the completed latent-space metric-compatibility and inverse-PLS OpenSpec changes.
  • Sync their capability specifications into the canonical OpenSpec specs.
  • Keep the M-value/PLS pilot report, inverse-study findings, configs, and reproduction commands linked from the documentation.
  • Record the current production contract: pooled PLS-DA, M-value methylation, fixed shared coordinate system, and per-statistic interpretation boundaries.

Exit gate: passed. A new contributor can locate and reproduce the current magnitude, orientation, shape, and inverse-interpretability evidence from the repository documentation.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Resolve shape invariance
docs.text:
Status: resolved on 2026-08-04; see Procrustes Shape Invariance Audit.

Purpose: determine whether the current nonzero shape response to rigid rotation is intended methodology or an estimator defect.

Work:

  • Create minimal two-dimensional configurations with known translation, uniform scaling, rigid rotation, reflection, and genuine bend transformations.
  • Compare MOTCO's GPA/Procrustes output against an analytic expectation and independent reference implementations such as SciPy and the original R procedure.
  • Isolate whether any discrepancy comes from centering, centroid-size normalization, rotation/reflection handling, iterative GPA, or the final distance calculation.
  • Add permanent invariance and regression tests.
  • If necessary, correct the estimator and document any behavioral change; otherwise rename/reinterpret the statistic so its actual invariants are explicit.

Exit gate: passed. Rigid translation, scaling, and proper rotation have documented expected outputs enforced by tests. The reflection policy was revisited on 2026-09-03 (unify-shape-reflection-policy): reflections are now aligned away at every ambient dimension, and mirror pairs score zero at full rank and above.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Audit orientation and shape constructions before integration
docs.text:
Status: resolved on 2026-08-05; see Realized Generator Geometry — Phase 2 Findings.

Purpose: separate generator cross-talk from integration or estimator cross-talk.

Work:

  • Measure every generated mode directly in the standardized pre-integration feature space.
  • For orientation, verify that the group trajectories differ primarily in normalized direction while path length and within-trajectory configuration remain controlled.
  • For shape, distinguish a free biological bend from a magnitude-matched bend; do not require a free bend to be magnitude- or orientation-neutral.
  • Retain magnitude as the positive control because it is already specific under M-value integration.
  • Add construction-level diagnostics to study outputs so each replicate records the realized pre-integration delta, angle, and shape—not only its requested mode/effect size.
  • Revise acceptance targets so they reflect achievable properties of the chosen constructions rather than an assumed perfectly diagonal specificity matrix.

Exit gate: passed. Each study mode has a documented realized geometry before PLS, and evaluation records analytic population, standardized population, observed standardized, and PLS-latent checkpoints. Orientation is pure in native methylation but mixed after biological cascade propagation; both shape constructions are documented as free/mixed bends rather than shape-specific interventions.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Implement production orientation-driver attribution
docs.text:
Purpose: turn a significant global orientation test into stable feature- and pathway-level interpretation.

For two stages, calculate standardized or covariate-adjusted feature transitions

d_A = LSmean(A, stage 2) - LSmean(A, stage 1)
d_B = LSmean(B, stage 2) - LSmean(B, stage 1)

and isolate direction from magnitude with

q_observed = d_B / ||d_B|| - d_A / ||d_A||.

Work:

  • Keep one pooled preprocessing and PLS model fixed for both groups.
  • Reconstruct each group-stage PLS displacement through the same fitted loadings and calculate q_PLS from the reconstructed normalized feature transitions.
  • Report q_observed, q_PLS, and their residual so users can see which directional difference PLS retained and omitted.
  • Attribution reports both decompositions for trajectories with more than two stages: the adjacent transitions, and the signed principal orientations that decompose the tested angle estimand, the latter qualified by a relative-eigengap degeneracy flag.
  • Bootstrap subjects within the appropriate design strata to estimate feature sign stability, rank stability, and top-k selection frequency.
  • Add correlated-feature module and pathway summaries; individual features should not be presented as stable drivers without bootstrap support.
  • Report standardized and original-unit effects separately.
  • Treat pooled VIP as supporting context only: VIP measures pooled importance for stage prediction, not group differences in normalized progression effects.

Exit gate: a significant orientation result can produce a reproducible driver report containing transition-specific features/modules, captured-versus-residual contrast, and uncertainty measures without refitting separate group latent spaces.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Repeat the medium pilot
docs.text:
Purpose: verify the corrected estimator/constructions before spending cluster time on the definitive study.

Recommended run:

  • PLS integration with M-value methylation
  • 300 samples and 4 stages
  • 50–100 replicates per cell
  • 199 permutations
  • Effects 0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, and 1.00
  • Modes: magnitude, orientation, shape, and translation
  • Matched seeds and construction-level realized-geometry diagnostics

Evaluate:

  • Per-statistic Type I error under none and translation controls
  • Magnitude/delta specificity and monotonic power
  • Orientation/angle power and monotonicity
  • Shape behavior under the interpretation established in Phase 1
  • Off-diagonal rejection rates alongside realized pre-integration geometry
  • Stability of PLS component count and attribution summaries

Exit gate: no unresolved implementation artifact; magnitude remains specific; orientation reaches an agreed power target with an interpretable curve; shape results match its validated invariance contract. If a target fails, revise the method or scientific claim—not merely the Monte Carlo sample size.

Status: HOLD (run 2026-08-27, full report). The pilot ran 1,900 work units with zero failures using examples/trajectory_power_study/phase4_pilot_100x199.json: 100 replicates, 199 permutations, n=300, four stages, matched seeds with a shared zero-effect anchor, and bounded orientation attribution.

What passed:

  • All eighteen predeclared Type I control tests. Translation leaves every statistic at nominal level at every effect size; the largest control rate anywhere was 0.09 against a bound of 0.0936.
  • Magnitude: delta power 1.00 throughout, with angle 0.01 and shape 0.00 at the top effect — the estimator is more specific than the construction, whose population angle is already 39.9°.
  • Shape: shape power 0.94–1.00, monotone. The corrected Procrustes estimator detects the constructed bend.
  • Diagnostics: selected PLS dimensionality was modally 3 in all 19 cells; all 400 eligible orientation replicates produced valid attribution.

What failed:

  • Orientation angle power is 0.65 at the top effect against the 0.80 floor — over three Monte Carlo standard errors short — and the curve is nearly flat across effects (0.59 → 0.65). The cause is not yet identified. The construction is strong and survives integration (81° at population, 57° in the latent space, against an 8.9° latent null floor), so a simple underpowered-signal account should not apply; and the records contradict it directly, since replicates that fail to reject have a larger mean observed angle (66.7°) than those that reject (52.5°). Latent dimensionality, weak construction, cross-talk, and Monte Carlo noise are all ruled out. More replicates would not fix it.

Update 2026-08-28 (report): an orientation sign-anchor defect was found and fixed — PC1's sign was anchored on the centered first-stage row, which flips for bent trajectories. It was a real bug, but it does not explain this failure. On byte-identical data corrected power is 0.64/0.64/0.67/0.68 across effects 0.25 → 1.00: ~3 points higher, still flat, still short of 0.80. The near-180° null mass is unchanged at 21/700, and the realized-geometry figures stand (81° population, 57° latent). The shortfall survives correction and remains unexplained.

Update 2026-09-01 (report): the shortfall is explained. Each replicate's own angle critical value regresses on its own observed angle with slope 0.811 — near-unit tracking, specific to angle (the same slope is 0.030 for delta and 0.058 for shape in the cells where those carry signal). That accounts for the inversion completely: the 32 non-rejecting orientation replicates carry a larger mean observed angle (60.8° vs 46.5°) but a 6.6× larger critical value (103.6° vs 15.8°). The tracking is not a defect to remove — a fixed threshold drops power from 0.68 to 0.01, and cross-replicate standardization gains only 0.02 — so the statistic and its test are sound, and the gap to 0.80 is a design-point property.

Two findings carry into Phase 5. Orientation→shape is the only response that first becomes material at the PLS checkpoint rather than in the population geometry. And the PLS reconstruction retains only ~6% of the observed orientation contrast (cosine 0.08), so its captured-component top-20 precision against generator truth is 0.15 while the observed component's is 1.00 — driver reports must use the observed component. Component selection saturates at n_stages - 1 because supervision is on the stage label, so a space sized for stage separation is not sized to preserve group orientation contrast.

Update 2026-09-02 (note): the quantity the pivotality report could not name — what makes one replicate resolvable and another not — is now recorded on every replicate. Each record carries the eigenspectrum of its centered latent stage-mean configuration (pooled and per group) and, when permutations run, the pooled relative eigengap over its own permutation draws. The study report stratifies orientation power by that eigengap and the pivotality analysis reports its association with the null width. It is a recorded covariate only: no statistic, p-value, permutation draw, or decision rule changed.

Before Phase 5, see the Phase 5 readiness worklist. Its blocking item — diagnosing the orientation shortfall — was resolved on 2026-09-01 by diagnose-angle-null-pivotality: the co-variation hypothesis is confirmed, it explains the inversion, no remedy recovers the power, and angle proceeds as specified. What remains: investigate orientation→shape at the PLS checkpoint, revisit latent dimensionality if orientation is a primary estimand, and then choose the Phase 5 design point — which now also owns the 0.80 orientation power floor.

Update 2026-09-08 (report): the design point is chosen and the floor is met, not revised. A crossed pilot (ρ ∈ {0, 0.5, 0.8} × n ∈ {300, 600, 1200}, p_dmp = 0.1, uncensored effect axis, 6,500 units, 0 failures) puts orientation angle power at 0.88 (1·SE lower bound 0.85) at ρ = 0, n = 1200, with that column's null at nominal level on every statistic. Sample size does what the pivotality report predicted — the angle null width contracts 40.7° → 18.8° → 10.8° along n at a constant eigengap — but baseline continuity does not help and is non-monotone (ρ = 0.5 is worse at every n), because the orientation surgery realizes a smaller latent contrast on a trending baseline. The Phase 5 claim is therefore n-conditional at the isotropic endpoint, reported beside the recorded eigengap (median 0.049). Selected rank stays at n_stages − 1 for every n, so the retained-rank question passes to readiness item 3 unchanged; magnitude and shape must be re-measured at the chosen point because p_dmp changed.

The July pilot (mvalue-pls-pilot-2026-07-30.md) predates the corrected shape estimator and realized-geometry diagnostics. It is retained unchanged as historical evidence and is superseded for Phase 4 gate purposes.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Paper-grade PLS operating-characteristic study
docs.text:
Purpose: produce the definitive evidence for publication and production guidance.

Planned baseline:

  • Design point chosen 2026-09-08 (report): ρ = 0 (independent baseline), n = 1200, four stages, p_dmp = 0.1, pooled PLS on M-value methylation
  • Rank rule committed 2026-09-08 (latent-rank ladder report): stage-supervised double cross-validation (plsda_doubleCV, modal LV, parsimony tie-break; group-blind), which selects rank 3 = n_stages − 1 at the design point. The predeclared ladder rule over fixed ranks {3, 4, 6, 9, 12} returned keep_cv: no rank gained orientation angle power (0.79–0.86 vs 0.85) and every rank above 3 lost shape/shape (1.00 → 0.57) and orientation shape/delta power while off-target angle responses rose. Magnitude and shape were re-measured there under CV (delta 1.00, shape ≥ 0.95).
  • 500 replicates per cell
  • 999 permutations per test
  • Resumable, sharded execution using examples/trajectory_power_study/phase5_power_study.json (study.json is the superseded historical config)
  • Predeclared acceptance targets and parameter signatures

Deliverables:

  • Per-statistic Type I tables and combined-rule Type I results
  • Power curves with Monte Carlo uncertainty
  • Mode-by-statistic response matrix interpreted against realized input geometry
  • Sensitivity analyses for sample size, retained PLS dimensions, signal density, and relevant nuisance settings
  • Runtime, failure, and reproducibility report
  • Paper-ready figures and a versioned study report tied to the exact code revision and configuration

Run status: executed 2026-09-10 as job 880599 on ing (19 cells × 500 replicates × 999 permutations = 9,500 units, 100 shards, 3 h 04 m wall, 182.7 core-hours, 0 failures, 0 censored surgeries). Gate decision HOLD on the two magnitude mandatory controls; all three mandatory power diagonals and all 21 Type I checks met. See the findings report and results/phase5-2026-09-10/. Magnitude re-measured 2026-10-08 under the joint construction as job 906705 (9 cells × 500 × 999 = 4,500 units, 2 h 06 m wall, 106.7 core-hours, 0 failures): reduced gate PROCEED — magnitude/delta 1.000 at the top with the rise resolved at 0.13 / 0.38 / 0.84 / 0.996 over e = 0.0025–0.02, magnitude/angle 0.024 and magnitude/shape 0.000 at e = 1.00, anchor byte-identical to the 2026-09-10 anchor at all 500 replicates. See the addendum, results/phase5-magnitude-2026-10-08/, the pilot results/phase5-magnitude-pilot-2026-10-08/, and the bracket results/magnitude-axis-bracket-2026-10-08/.

Exit gate: conclusions are stable at paper-grade Monte Carlo precision, all deviations from preregistered targets are explained, and the report distinguishes statistical operating characteristics from biological construction cross-talk. CLOSED 2026-09-10 as a conditional pass (exit review): all three criteria met; the Phase 4 gate's HOLD stands as recorded and resolves to a construction defect with a known fix; the magnitude specificity claim, withheld pending re-measurement of the corrected construction, was lifted on 2026-10-08 for the joint construction (addendum) — stated as "specific and conservative", and construction-specific until the default is flipped.

docs.title: Phase 6 — Real-data case study
docs.text:
Purpose: demonstrate that the validated method answers a meaningful biological question end to end.

Work:

  • Predefine cohorts, stages, covariates, missing-data handling, and preprocessing. (Case-study repository. motco analyze takes the stage order and block units as explicit inputs and does no normalization, filtering or imputation; donor covariates and the missing-covariate policy are explicit inputs since 0.8.0, and covariate-aware latent construction (--latent-adjustment) is opt-in since 0.9.0.)
  • Fit one pooled, cross-validated PLS representation. (MOTCO: motco analyze, real-data-trajectory-analysis.)
  • Report magnitude, orientation, and validated shape results with uncertainty. (MOTCO: motco analyze statistics, RRPP p-values and null summary.)
  • For significant orientation, produce observed and PLS-reconstructed feature contrasts, bootstrap stability, and pathway/module enrichment. (MOTCO: motco analyze --attribution for contrasts and bootstrap stability; pathway/module enrichment stays in the case-study repository.)
  • Include sensitivity to PLS dimensionality and preprocessing choices. (Dimensionality: MOTCO, motco analyze --forced-components. Preprocessing choices: case-study repository.)
  • Make the analysis reproducible from raw-input contracts to final figures. (MOTCO writes the analysis artifact; raw inputs and figures live in the case-study repository.)

Exit gate: collaborators can trace each global trajectory claim to stable feature/module drivers and reproduce the result from documented inputs and configuration.

Case study. SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus astrocytes, with donor-level RNA + ATAC pseudobulks. Sex is the group and ADNC is merged into three stages (Not AD + Low / Intermediate / High). The primary cohort is the ≥30-nuclei cohort (n = 80: F 11/10/28, M 9/10/12); the ≥50-nuclei cohort (n = 74) is a sensitivity analysis. SEA-AD preprocessing and the real-data analysis live in the external case-study repository, Omnia-Lab-UC/sead_sexdiff. MOTCO supplies the method and the operating characteristics below. The case-study analysis must pin MOTCO to the revision that merges phase6-small-n-operating-study. The operating study itself ran at 5325f6d (records) and 946e471 (report), with motco 0.6.0, numpy 2.3.5, scikit-learn 1.8.0, scipy 1.16.3 and python 3.11.16.

Small-n operating study — done 2026-10-09 (report). This is the precondition the Phase 5 exit review set before any SEA-AD result can be interpreted. MOTCO gained explicit group × stage sample sizes (group_stage_sizes) and evaluation-time block selection (integration_params.layers); both are byte-identical when absent. - A pilot (results/phase6-small-n-pilot-2026-10-09/, 3,500 units) fixed the effect axes. - The paper-grade run was split into a magnitude profile and an orientation/shape/translation profile, 500 × 999 each, over a four-column design grid (cohort size × block count). That is 42,000 units, 150 core-hours and 0 failures (results/phase6-small-n-magnitude-2026-10-09/, results/phase6-small-n-2026-10-09/). - Advisory gates: magnitude PROCEED; orientation/shape HOLD, because both power floors are missed (0.300 / 0.228). Per design D6 this revises the claim, not the method.

Orientation measurement probe — done 2026-10-12 (report, results/orientation-measurement-probe-2026-10-12/). This probe asked why orientation is weak at n = 80. It crossed five measurement spaces with two orientation estimators on matched seeds, at the Phase 6 and Phase 5 designs: 1,000 units, 10 arms each, 28 core-hours, 0 failures. MOTCO gained the opt-in orientation_estimator (net_displacement) and the diagnostic pca / pls_within_group integration methods, all byte-identical when unused. - Under the predeclared rule no arm advances. - pls_cv × net_displacement fails only the anchor criterion (Phase 6 0.100 vs bound 0.0936), with a large orientation gain and no power or specificity loss. - A fixed-basis pls_within_group is invalid without a refit (anchor up to 0.88). - pca and forced rank 2(K − 1) lose Phase 6 shape power. - A baseline-continuity (ρ) sweep at the Phase 6 design was considered first and dropped: the Phase 5 design-point pilot already showed that ρ does not buy orientation power, and the probe places the loss in the measurement. - Production defaults are unchanged, and the case-study interpretability statement above stands.

Net-displacement Type I study — done 2026-10-13 (report, results/net-displacement-type-i-2026-10-13/). The paper-grade estimator comparison's (Next changes item 2) anchor-only step: the zero-effect anchor and the translation control at 500 × 999, at both designs, across five matched columns (pls_cv × pc1, and pls_cv, forced rank 2(K − 1), pca, concat × net displacement). 12,000 units, 133 core-hours, 0 failures. MOTCO gained the explicit design-grid form (design_grid.points), the advisory acceptance.anchor_decision rule and scripts/net_displacement_follow_up.py, all byte-identical when unused. - Every net-displacement column holds the bound 0.0695 on delta, angle and shape at both designs; the lead arm's anchor angle is 0.050 at both. - The follow-up rule selects paper_grade_power_comparison; the anchor-excess diagnosis is not needed. - Under net displacement the translation control's angle rate is close to the bound (lead arm 0.068 at Phase 6; concat 0.078), so the comparison must hold it to that bound. - The baseline column reproduces the Phase 6 and Phase 5 parent records (same seeds and RRPP seed): p-values identical in 2,000/2,000 records.

Net-displacement power comparison — done 2026-10-14 (report, results/net-displacement-power-2026-10-14/). Formerly Next changes item 2: pls_cv × net_displacement against pls_cv × pc1 at 500 × 999, four modes at e = 0.25–1.0, at both designs, on matched datasets and permutation draws. 36,000 units, 384 core-hours, 0 failures. MOTCO gained the advisory acceptance.column_decision rule, scripts/net_displacement_power_follow_up.py and scripts/net_displacement_power_checks.py, all byte-identical when unused. - The candidate qualifies at both designs: orientation/angle at e = 1.0 rises from 0.300 to 0.648 at Phase 6 (gain, +0.348 against a 0.059 threshold) and from 0.840 to 0.924 at Phase 5 (no_loss). Anchor angle 0.050 at both. - Every mandatory control is within 0.0695, which PC1 does not achieve: shape → angle 0.054 / 0.022 (PC1 0.138 / 0.796), magnitude → angle 0.030 / 0.000, translation → angle 0.068 / 0.040 (Phase 6 one rejection under the bound). - The cross-design rule selects adopt_net_displacement. Its follow-up, the harness-default flip, is done (default-net-displacement-orientation, 2026-10-15). - At Phase 6 the eigengap no longer gates orientation power (low tercile 0.114 → 0.731), but the CV-selected rank still does at the construction maximum (0.280 at rank ≤ 3, 0.996 above), and power is 0.084–0.178 at e ≤ 0.75. - delta and shape p-values are identical between the two columns in 17,000/17,000 paired records, and the baseline column reproduces 15,500 parent records with 0 seed or p-value mismatches.

The report's binding interpretability statement for the case study: - delta. A rejection is evidence that the trajectories differ; it is consistent with a size difference but does not exclude a direction or shape difference. A non-rejection argues only against size differences of about 25 % or more. - angle and shape. A rejection is evidence that the trajectories differ, but not of which kind. A non-rejection is uninformative at n = 80. - angle (net displacement, revised 2026-10-15). With net displacement the harness default (default-net-displacement-orientation), the angle statement is the one in the power comparison report §7. angle is the angle between the groups' net displacement vectors (last stage mean − first stage mean) in the latent space, so it reads only the endpoint stages. A rejection is evidence that the groups' net directions of change differ: Type I is controlled (anchor 0.050), and the size, shape and location constructions stay within the bound (0.024–0.068). Translation sits at 0.058–0.068, near the bound, so a rejection alongside a location difference warrants care. A non-rejection is uninformative at n = 80: power is 0.084–0.178 at e ≤ 0.75, and 0.648 at the construction maximum (0.280 when CV retains three or fewer components, 0.996 above). - Selected rank. The cohort's CV-selected PLS rank replaces its eigengap as the covariate reported beside any angle result; under net displacement the eigengap no longer conditions the statement.

Covariate-aware latent construction — implemented 2026-10-20, validation runs pending (covariate-aware-latent-construction, MOTCO 0.9.0; API). In both SEA-AD cohorts CV selected rank 1, so angle was 0° by construction. The single component turned out to be a donor-level library-quality axis: Spearman −0.84 with the astrocyte nuclei's ribosomal-protein UMI fraction, against +0.49 with stage. The 0.8.0 covariates adjust the stage means exactly within the basis but never touch which basis is chosen. Label-blind residualization upstream removed the axis but also the stage signal collinear with it (held-out CV AUROC 0.63 → 0.41). covariate_latent_adjustment (stage | group_stage) instead residualizes the features on the declared covariates conditional on the stage, or group × stage, indicators, with per-training-set coefficients inside the CV, folds stratified on the conditioning cells, and the pooled scale kept. It measures the raw features in the new basis, so only the basis and the CV rank change. Without the setting every output equals 0.8.0. The local smoke run of the Type I check (R = 20, 99 permutations) calibrated the nuisance injection: the unadjusted basis's first component tracks the covariate at median |ρ| 0.815 with s_z = 40, against 0.64 at the covariate check's s_z = 3. In the residualized arms that falls to about 0.32. The paper-grade Type I check (2026-10-20, report) returned adopt_stage: stage held delta 0.031, angle 0.067 and shape 0.058 against 0.0706; group_stage exceeded on angle (0.082). The power comparison (2026-10-20, report) returned candidate_fails for both conditionings. stage gains orientation power (angle 0.922 against 0.784 with the nuisance axis, 0.931 against 0.642 without), but loses shape power with the axis (0.243 against 0.428) and small-magnitude power without it. Its translation angle control, like the covariate-blind basis's, sits above the bound. group_stage loses most orientation and shape power. The case study may therefore use --latent-adjustment stage only, as a sensitivity analysis beside the 0.8.0 covariate-adjusted analysis, under both reports' conditions. It must first justify the covariate set in its own proposal (the mediator limitation).

docs.title: Phase 7 — Optional SNF-native trajectory methodology
docs.text:
Purpose: use SNF according to graph geometry rather than forcing Euclidean MOTCO statistics onto spectral coordinates.

This is not on the critical path for the PLS production workflow.

Status: deferred, and the question is closed rather than pending (Phase 5 exit review, §5). Nothing in the paper-grade run or the magnitude-construction diagnostic bears on SNF — the study measured the PLS latent space throughout and concat appeared only as a baseline — so the deferral does not await further Phase 5 evidence. It awaits a decision to define graph-native path-length and angle statistics, which is independent work.

Candidate work:

  • Define group-stage states on one pooled fused graph.
  • Evaluate diffusion or resistance path length as a magnitude analogue.
  • Compare transition profiles or diffusion flows as an orientation analogue.
  • Compare normalized stage-by-stage diffusion-distance matrices as a configuration analogue.
  • Design a permutation scheme that rebuilds or conditions on the graph without invalidating exchangeability.
  • Validate every proposed graph statistic on controlled nonlinear manifolds before exposing it as production functionality.

Exit gate: an SNF-specific statistic has a clear graph-native estimand, calibrated Type I error, controlled power behavior, and no claim of preserving original feature-space Euclidean geometry.

docs.title: Cross-cutting engineering work
docs.text:
These items support every scientific phase:

  • Preserve fitted preprocessing, PLS model, component count, feature order, and loadings as a versioned analysis artifact. For real data, motco.analysis.write_analysis_outputs (motco analyze --out-dir) writes result.json, latent scores, PLS loadings and latent stage means. It records units, the feature order signature and software versions, and pickles no estimator.
  • Record seeds, configurations, parameter signatures, software versions, and failed replicates in every study.
  • Keep fast deterministic invariance tests separate from slow operating-characteristic studies.
  • Add CI coverage for core geometry invariants and study-config validation.
  • Prefer structured CSV/JSON outputs plus concise Markdown reports over findings that exist only in notebooks.
  • Keep public documentation synchronized with methodological decisions and archived OpenSpec findings.
  • Decide the fate of the committed toy fixture (examples/data/toy/, deferred from docs-sync-audit, 2026-09-04). The fixture predates the numpy generator: its truth.json records intersim_metadata and omits n_stages, p_dmp, and baseline_continuity, and running the current motco simulate at the same seed produces a different dataset. docs-sync-audit corrected the documentation — the toy-dataset spec now describes the fixture as pinned rather than regenerable — but did not resolve the underlying question: regenerate the example data with the numpy generator so the tutorial exercises the shipped code path, or keep it pinned as a historical artifact. Regenerating touches committed example data, examples/motco_example.ipynb, the toy-dataset spec scenarios, and tests/test_toy_dataset.py, so it needs its own change.

docs.title: Explicitly deferred
docs.text:
• Expanding SNF use before graph-native metrics are defined
  • Reading the pooled orientation power figure as applicable at any eigengap
  • Claiming angle or shape specificity against the methylation-only all magnitude construction (its controls fail; the claim holds for joint only — addendum)
  • Interpreting pooled VIP scores as orientation drivers
  • Fitting separate, unaligned PLS spaces per group
  • Claiming that a latent-space reconstruction is a unique or causal molecular inverse
  • Optimizing performance before the statistic and construction contracts are settled

docs.title: Next changes
docs.text:
The magnitude_kind default flip, formerly item 1, is done (default-joint-magnitude-construction, 2026-10-09): joint is the generator and motco simulate default, and the ten historical configs pin "all" with their parameter signatures checked against a pre-flip fixture (tests/test_magnitude_default_pins.py).

The one-sided acceptance bound, formerly item 2, is done (one-sided-acceptance-targets, 2026-10-14). Each acceptance.type_i and acceptance.specificity entry takes bound: two_sided (the default, unchanged) or upper, which is the gate's rate ≤ α + k·√(α(1 − α)/R) and shares its implementation. No committed config opts in, so every committed report/ regenerates byte-identically.

The paper-grade estimator comparison, formerly item 2, is done (net-displacement-power-comparison, 2026-10-14; report) and selected adopt_net_displacement. It ran no concat column, so concat's p-padding question stays open; concat remains the ceiling reference only.

The orientation-estimator default flip, formerly item 2, is done (default-net-displacement-orientation, 2026-10-15): SimulationEvaluationParams.orientation_estimator defaults to net_displacement, every committed config and historical diagnostic pins "pc1", and the configs' signatures and matched seeds are checked against a pre-flip fixture (tests/test_orientation_default_pins.py). The stats primitives (estimate_difference, RRPP) keep PC1 as their default. No compute was needed.

  1. Run the Phase 6 real-data case study in Omnia-Lab-UC/sead_sexdiff. The orientation-estimator default flip unblocked it. The real-data-trajectory-analysis change (MOTCO 0.7.0) removed the last MOTCO-side blocker: the case study must run its trajectory analysis through motco analyze (or motco.analysis.analyze_trajectories; API) and pin the MOTCO release that contains it. That entry point is the harness's production measurement on caller-supplied blocks. A regression test checks it against the harness on identical data. It defaults to the net-displacement estimator, requires an explicit stage order and records the selected rank, null summary and spectrum, so no estimator argument has to be passed by hand. Do not assemble the analysis from motco plsr + motco de or from the stats primitives: they are a different pipeline, and the primitives and motco de default to PC1. The small-n operating study (report) and the revised angle statement (Phase 6 above, from the power comparison report §7) are binding. Report the cohort's CV-selected rank beside any angle result as the covariate; the record carries it. Treat angle and shape non-rejections as uninformative, and treat a delta rejection as evidence of a difference, not specifically of size. Carry the structural-analogue limitation (InterSIM blocks, 498 measured features). Covariate adjustment landed in MOTCO 0.8.0 (item 2 below, done) with a covariates_validated Type I decision, so the case study may declare donor covariates in motco analyze under the conditions of the covariate Type I report §5, and must pin MOTCO ≥ 0.8.0 to do so. Its preprocessing and export (mtg-astrocyte-motco-export in sead_sexdiff) produce TMM log2-CPM blocks without chrX/Y/M, the top 5,000 variable features per block, and a donor covariate table: age at death (with a 90+ flag), PMI, RIN, years and level of education, and astrocyte nuclei counts per omic.
  2. Covariate-adjusted trajectories in motco analyze — done (covariate-adjusted-trajectories, MOTCO 0.8.0, 2026-10-16). TrajectoryDataset takes covariate_cols, categorical_covariates and missing_covariates; motco analyze takes --covariate, --categorical-covariate and --missing-covariates (API). The Phase 6 Type I check returned covariates_validated: adjusted delta 0.040, angle 0.062, shape 0.034 against the bound 0.0695, while the unadjusted arm rejected shape at 0.364 (report). Without covariates every output is byte-identical to 0.7.0. The original scope follows. The case study needs donor covariates inside the trajectory regression. MOTCO should own this because covariates enter the model: the LS-mean fit and the RRPP reduced model both change, and so does what is permuted. Scope:
  3. covariates in the full and reduced models;
  4. stage-mean LS-means evaluated at fixed covariate values (e.g. the pooled mean), recorded;
  5. an explicit missing-covariate policy, either error or complete-case, chosen by the caller, recorded, and never imputed;
  6. the covariate design recorded in result.json;
  7. a Type I check at the Phase 6 design with covariates that are correlated with group and stage. Absent covariates must stay byte-identical to 0.7.0.

Scope boundary for MOTCO preprocessing (decided 2026-10-16). The test is whether a step touches the model or the permutation null. - Normalization stays upstream. It is omic-specific, and when it is blind to the labels it changes what is measured, not the validity of the test. It is covered by the case study's preprocessing sensitivity analysis. - Label-blind feature filtering stays upstream. Supervised filtering (by group or stage) would bias the null unless it were repeated inside every permutation, so MOTCO documents it as forbidden rather than offering it. - Imputation stays upstream. The finite-values contract stays. Missing covariates are the only exception, and they are handled by the explicit policy above. 3. Covariate-aware latent construction: validation runs (covariate-aware-latent-construction, MOTCO 0.9.0). (a) The Type I check, scripts/latent_adjustment_type_i_check.py — done 2026-10-20 (report, results/latent-adjustment-type-i-2026-10-20/): 500 × 999, 5.1 core-hours, adopt_stage; group_stage is not admissible (angle 0.082 against 0.0703). (b) The power comparison — done 2026-10-20 (report, results/latent-adjustment-power-2026-10-20/), 158 core-hours, advisory candidate_fails for both arms — scripts/latent_adjustment_power_comparison.py: nuisance and clean columns × anchor, translation and three modes at four effects, 500 × 999 (14,000 units of three analyses, about 350 core-hours from the smoke timing), writing latent_adjustment_power_decision.json with the per-arm rank distributions. Each gets a dated report under docs/reports/ carrying the mediator limitation. In the Type I run, 52 stage and 38 group_stage replicates lost the arm to a rare categorical level dropping out of a CV training set; such replicates are recorded as unavailable. 4. The rank-1 angle degeneracy — done (minimum-latent-rank, MOTCO 0.10.0, 2026-10-23; report, results/rank-floor-2026-10-23/). CV could select rank 1, where angle is 0° or 180° by construction and its RRPP null is a two-point distribution, while forced_components required ≥ 2; both SEA-AD cohorts selected rank 1. The production latent space (fit_pls_latent_space, shared by the harness and motco analyze) now selects the rank from candidates at or above a floor of 2 (min_components=2; 1 restores the 0.9.0 rule and is the hash-omitted spelling, so every committed config, fixture and dated report reproduces under its min_components: 1 pin). The 0.9.0 power comparison's Phase 6 construction never selected rank 1, so the check weakened the per-omic stage effect (delta_* = 0.05 and 0.1 against the Phase 6 value 2.0, p_dmp unchanged) until the unfloored rule selected rank 1 in 58 % and 42 % of null replicates (held-out CV AUROC 0.52 and 0.58, the SEA-AD cohorts' 0.63–0.66 regime), and ran two matched arms (min_components 1 and 2) per unit at 500 × 999 over 14 cells at each strength (two 7,000-unit arrays, 99 core-hours). Both runs returned adopt_floor: the floor-2 arm holds the 0.0695 bound at the anchor (delta 0.042 / 0.044, angle 0.054 / 0.060, shape 0.036 / 0.038) and at the translation control (0.036 / 0.036, 0.046 / 0.042, 0.026 / 0.030). The floor-1 arm's rank-1 units had angle exactly 0° or 180° with a two-point null that never rejected (anchor angle 0.030 / 0.038), which is the degeneracy removed. Power is at the null in both arms at these strengths (the construction has almost no stage signal by design), so the floor defines angle and shape; it does not make them powerful, and the record's config_spectrum eigengap and null_summary say how resolvable orientation is in each analysis. sead_sexdiff reruns both cohorts at the floor in its own proposal and pins 0.10.0. 5. Consider optional block weighting. motco analyze z-scores each feature and concatenates the blocks unweighted, so a block's influence grows with its feature count. The SEA-AD export works around this by forcing equal N (5,000 + 5,000). How blocks are weighted is a property of the joint measurement rather than of one omic, so it is the one preprocessing step that belongs in MOTCO. Candidates are multiblock-PLS-style 1/√p_b scaling or unit total block variance. Weighting changes the latent space, so it is opt-in, byte-identical when absent, and needs its own Type I and power check before the case study may use it. It is separate from item 2. 6. Consider defaulting the null-dispersion materiality rule. Opt-in today so the committed Phase 5 report/ keeps regenerating byte-identically; switching the default is a reporting change needing a recorded re-issue of affected localization output.

docs.title: Real-Data Trajectory Analysis
docs.text:
motco.analysis runs the measurement the simulation studies validated on your own data: pooled per-feature standardization, a stage-supervised PLS-DA latent space with the double-CV rank rule, delta / angle / shape between two groups in that space with the net-displacement orientation estimator, and RRPP p-values. analyze_trajectories is the Python entry point and motco analyze the command-line one; both write the same analysis artifact.

Use this entry point rather than assembling motco plsr + motco de by hand. Those commands are a different pipeline: they skip the M-value contract, choose the rank without the parsimony tie-break, measure angle with PC1 by default, and record neither the selected rank, the null summary nor the spectrum.

docs.title: Input contract
docs.text:
• Blocks. One or more named omic blocks, each a samples × features table with string feature names. Blocks are concatenated in the order you declare them, and every joint feature is named "{block}__{feature}". Rows must equal the metadata's sample ids in the same order; every block needs at least one feature and only finite values.
  • Units. Each block declares a unit transform: identity (the default) or beta_to_mvalue (the logit of methylation beta values; values must lie in the open interval (0, 1)). MOTCO does not normalize counts, filter features or impute values. Supply blocks in the continuous units you want measured, for example log-normalized pseudobulk expression. The record states each block's declared units.
  • Metadata. A sample-id column, a group column with exactly two labels and a stage column, all named by you. Every group × stage cell must be observed.

  • Stage order. Required and explicit. Net displacement runs from the first to the last declared stage, and shape, the spectrum and every table follow this order. Stage order is never inferred by sorting labels, because High < Intermediate < Low alphabetically. Group order is optional and defaults to the labels sorted as strings.

  • Covariates (optional). covariate_cols names metadata columns, in model order; see Covariates.

Violations raise TrajectoryAnalysisError (a ValueError) naming the block, labels or cell at fault.

docs.title: What is measured and recorded
docs.text:
The latent space is fitted once on all samples, with the rank chosen by double cross-validation (the modal rank across outer repeats, the smaller rank winning ties) from the candidate ranks at or above the rank floor, min_components=2 by default (CLI --min-components), so angle and shape are measured in a space of at least two dimensions. min_components=1 restores the unfloored 0.9.0 rule and reproduces every 0.9.0 record and table byte for byte; a floor below 1 is rejected before anything is fitted. The CV defaults are the ones the operating studies ran: cv2_splits=4, cv1_splits=3, n_repeats=5, max_components=20, random_state=1203, each clamped to what the smallest stage can support (max_components to at least the floor plus one; a sample that cannot satisfy the floor is an error naming the counts). forced_components fixes the rank and skips cross-validation for the dimensionality sensitivity analysis, ignoring the floor; the record then says component_selection: "forced".

record (written as result.json) holds:

Key Contents statistics, p_values delta, angle, shape and their RRPP p-values (shape is null with two stages) null_summary per statistic: retained draws, mean, sd, 50/90/95/99 % quantiles of the permutation null config_spectrum eigenspectrum of the latent stage-mean configuration, pooled and per group, plus the permutation eigengap summary latent selected_lv, component_selection, CV settings (min_components beside them when the floor is above 1), cv_mean_auroc, feature counts, feature_order_signature design group and ordered stage levels, cell sizes per group × stage, contrast, analysed sample count covariates only when covariates are declared: names, kinds, factor levels and reference levels, design columns, the LS-mean reference row, missing policy, dropped samples, coefficients per latent component blocks each block's name, feature count, transform and units measurement orientation estimator, selected rank, permutations, seed, runtime params, software resolved parameters; MOTCO, numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas and Python versions attribution the compact attribution record, or a not_requested marker

The selected rank sits beside the angle result because orientation is only interpretable relative to the space it was measured in. The null summary shows how wide the observed statistic's own null was, and the relative eigengap in the spectrum indicates whether a group's orientation is resolvable at all.

The floor guarantees two dimensions, not a second axis with signal. Under the unfloored rule a weak stage signal makes every candidate rank tie near an AUROC of 0.5 and parsimony selects rank 1, where the two groups' orientations are parallel or antiparallel by construction, angle is 0° or 180°, its RRPP null is a two-point distribution, and collinear stage means carry no bend for shape; both SEA-AD cohorts selected rank 1. With the floor, when the stage signal supports one component the second is the best of the remaining candidates, and angle's null widens accordingly. Read the record's config_spectrum relative eigengap and null_summary.angle together: they say how resolvable orientation is in each analysis. The floor was validated on a small-n construction calibrated to select rank 1 by scripts/rank_floor_check.py (rank_floor_decision.json), with the floor-1 arm reported beside it: the 2026-10-23 run returned adopt_floor at both calibrated strengths (report), with power at the null in both arms, so the floor defines angle and shape without making them powerful.

docs.title: Equivalence to the simulation harness
docs.text: analyze_trajectories and evaluate_semisynthetic_trajectory(..., integration_method="pls") call the same block-scaling cores and the same fit_pls_latent_space. On identical data, stage order and settings, the rank floor included, they return the same latent matrix, statistics, p-values, selected rank, null summary and spectrum. tests/test_analysis.py checks this for the default estimator, PC1 and a two-block layer selection.

docs.title: Attribution
docs.text: With attribution=AttributionDiagnosticSettings(enabled=True, ...) (CLI: --attribution), frozen-model orientation attribution runs on the fitted pooled estimator and the standardized joint matrix it was fitted to, with your stage order and group labels. The latent space is not refitted. Real data carry no generator truth, so the truth-recovery block is reported unavailable rather than invented. The full tables are written under attribution/.

docs.title: Analysis artifact
docs.text:
write_analysis_outputs(result, out_dir) writes:

  • result.json: the record above.
  • latent_scores.csv: samples × pls_*, indexed by sample id.
  • pls_loadings.csv: block, feature, pls_* (the PLS x_rotations_, in joint order).
  • stage_means.csv: group, stage, pls_*, the fitted latent LS-mean vectors in declared stage order. Pass these to motco.viz.plot_trajectories.
  • attribution/*.csv, when attribution ran.

It refuses to replace an existing result.json unless overwrite=True (CLI: --overwrite). The fitted scikit-learn estimator is not pickled, because pickles are version-fragile. The scores, loadings and recorded feature order signature are enough to audit and re-project the fit.

docs.title: Covariates
docs.text:
Donor covariates such as age at death, PMI or RIN enter the trajectory regression in the latent space, so the stage means, the RRPP reduced model and therefore what is permuted all account for them. Declare them on the dataset:

dataset = TrajectoryDataset(
    ...,
    covariate_cols=["age_at_death", "pmi", "education_level"],
    categorical_covariates=["education_level"],   # optional; non-numeric columns are categorical anyway
    missing_covariates="complete_case",           # default "error"
)

CLI: --covariate age_at_death --covariate pmi --categorical-covariate education_level --missing-covariates complete_case.

  • Coding. A numeric (non-boolean) column enters as one design column holding its values. Any other column, or one listed in categorical_covariates (for numeric-coded factors), enters as drop-first indicators name[level], with levels ordered as strings (numerically when every label is an integer); the first level is the reference.
  • Model. The full model is group × stage + covariates and the reduced model group + stage + covariates. Covariates are additive: no interaction with group or stage. RRPP permutes the reduced model's residuals as before, so every permuted dataset keeps the fitted covariate effects.
  • LS-means. Every group × stage mean is evaluated at the pooled mean of each covariate design column (for a factor, its observed level proportions). The covariate term then adds the same vector to every stage mean, and delta, angle and shape are translation-invariant, so the statistics do not depend on the reference. Only stage_means.csv does, and the record states the reference row.
  • Missing values. missing_covariates="error" (the default) rejects any missing covariate value, naming the column and up to ten samples. "complete_case" drops those samples from the metadata and every block before standardization, the latent fit and the design, and records the dropped ids. A deletion that empties a group × stage cell is an error. Covariates are never imputed; blocks must still be complete.
  • Guards. A covariate that is also the sample, group or stage column, a constant numeric covariate, a factor with one observed level, a non-finite numeric value, and a model with covariates that is not of full column rank (for example a covariate collinear with group × stage) are rejected with an error naming the covariate(s).

By default the latent space is covariate-blind, and the adjustment is still exact. PLS-DA is fitted on the standardized features against stage alone, exactly as without covariates, so the latent scores, loadings and selected rank do not change. OLS commutes with a fixed linear map: regressing the scores T = XW on [design, covariates] gives the coefficients of regressing X on the same design, projected by W. The stage means are therefore adjusted exactly as in feature space; only the basis W was chosen without the covariates. If a covariate effect is large and aligned with stage, PLS may spend a component on it; latent adjustment chooses the basis with the covariates instead.

Attribution is not available with covariates. Frozen-model attribution works from unadjusted cell means, so a request for both raises an error before any fitting.

Keep the covariate set parsimonious. Small cells (the SEA-AD MTG design has 9–28 donors per cell) and many covariate columns can make the model near-singular or the null unstable. The record's design_columns states the degrees of freedom used.

Type I validation. scripts/covariate_type_i_check.py measures size at the Phase 6 design with covariates confounded with group, stage and their interaction (adjusted vs unadjusted arms on a shared latent fit); see the report. Report covariate-adjusted results only under its covariates_validated decision.

Without covariates the record, the artifact and every output are identical to MOTCO 0.7.0 (except the runtime); the covariates key is absent and the schema version is unchanged (tests/test_analysis_identity.py).

docs.title: Latent adjustment
docs.text:
With covariates declared, the PLS-DA basis is still fitted on the features alone. A large technical axis aligned with stage (library quality, for example) can then take a whole component, and at a selected rank of 1 or 2 that leaves little room for the biology. covariate_latent_adjustment (CLI: --latent-adjustment) fits the basis on features residualized on the declared covariates instead:

params = TrajectoryAnalysisParams(permutations=999, seed=1, covariate_latent_adjustment="stage")

motco analyze ... --covariate age_at_death --covariate pmi --latent-adjustment stage
  • Conditional residualization. Every pooled-standardized joint feature is regressed on [1, D, C], where C holds the declared covariate design columns and D the conditioning design, and only the fitted covariate part C γ is subtracted. Under stage, D is the drop-first stage indicators; under group_stage, the group, stage and group × stage indicators. By Frisch–Waugh–Lovell, γ is the covariates' within-design effect, so stage signal that is merely correlated with a covariate stays in the features. Residualizing on the covariates alone would remove it: label-blind residualization upstream of MOTCO dropped the case study's held-out CV AUROC from 0.63 to 0.41. stage keeps the group label out of the basis; under group_stage the group enters only through the pooled within-cell slope. Use stage: it is the conditioning the Type I check admitted (see below).
  • Leak-free cross-validation. Inside the double CV, every outer rest set and inner training set estimates its own γ and residualizes its held-out samples as X_held_out − C_held_out γ, so held-out labels never enter the residualization. Both CV levels stratify their folds on the conditioning cells (stages under stage, group × stage cells under group_stage), so every training set can estimate the conditioning design. Under stage the folds equal those of the unadjusted analysis. The final basis uses γ estimated on all samples.
  • The pooled scale is kept. The residualized features are not re-standardized: every PLS fit on this path uses scale=False. A feature whose variance was mostly covariate is down-weighted, not inflated back to unit variance, and when the covariate effects are weak the basis approaches the unadjusted one.
  • The raw features are measured in the new basis. The latent scores are the pooled-standardized features (not the residuals), centered at the residuals' mean and projected onto the basis. The trajectory model, the LS-means, the RRPP reduced model and the permutations are exactly those of the covariate-adjusted analysis above. With the covariates in both RRPP models, projecting the raw or the residualized features gives identical statistics, p-values and null draws, because the difference (C − C̄) γ W lies in the models' column space. So only the choice of basis (and of CV rank) changes. Measuring the raw features keeps the covariates block's coefficients and stage_means.csv on the same footing as without the setting.
  • The same covariates in both places. The residualization covariates are exactly covariate_cols, which also enter the trajectory model; that equality is what makes the projection choice immaterial. To residualize on technical variables, declare them as covariates.
  • Guards. The setting without covariates is an error before any fitting. The full-sample residualization design must have full column rank, otherwise the error names the covariates and the conditioning. Every CV training design must too, otherwise the error names the repeat and fold; this happens when a rare factor level drops out of a training set, and depends on random_state. Merge rare levels upstream rather than relying on a minimum-norm fit, whose held-out shift would be arbitrary. Attribution stays unavailable with covariates.
  • Record. result.json gains a latent_adjustment block after covariates, and latent.integration_params.latent_adjustment names the conditioning. The block holds conditioning, covariates, design_columns (conditioning then covariate columns, beyond the intercept), n_samples, residual_df (n − 1 − k − q), cv_min_training_df (the smallest training-set residual df seen in CV; null with forced_components), feature_scale (pooled_standardized) and feature_r2. That last field summarizes each feature's partial R² of the covariates given the intercept and conditioning (5/25/50/75/95 % quantiles, mean, fraction above 0.5), the share of variance the residualization removes. params.covariate_latent_adjustment is recorded only when set.

Mediator limitation. Residualizing a variable that mediates the stage effect removes real signal, and no simulation can tell a confounder from a mediator. Choosing and justifying the covariate set is the analysis's job, not MOTCO's: a technical variable that is itself downstream of disease stage (a cell-quality metric that worsens with pathology, say) is a mediator candidate.

Validation. scripts/latent_adjustment_type_i_check.py measures size at the Phase 6 design under a covariate-aligned nuisance axis calibrated so that the unadjusted basis spends its first component on it (median |Spearman| ≥ 0.8). It runs three arms per replicate (unadjusted basis, stage, group_stage) at 8 declared covariates, and its decision file names the admissible conditionings (adopt_stage | adopt_group_stage | diagnose_latent_excess). The 2026-10-20 run returned adopt_stage (report). stage held delta 0.031, angle 0.067 and shape 0.058 against 0.0706. group_stage exceeded the bound on angle (0.082) and is not admissible. About 10 % of replicates lost an arm to a rare factor level. scripts/latent_adjustment_power_comparison.py compares power with and without such an axis against the unadjusted basis. Its 2026-10-20 run (report) returned candidate_fails for both conditionings. stage raised orientation power (angle 0.92–0.93 against 0.64–0.78 at the top effect) but lost shape power when the nuisance axis was present, and small-magnitude power without it. group_stage lost most orientation and shape power. Residualizing on covariates confounded with the design removes signal even when they have no effect. Report latent-adjusted results only with stage conditioning, as a sensitivity analysis beside the covariate-adjusted analysis rather than as a replacement, under the conditions of both reports.

Without the setting, every output is identical to MOTCO 0.8.0 except the runtime, record["params"] included (tests/test_analysis_identity.py).

docs.title: Example: SEA-AD-style design
docs.text:
Two blocks (RNA and ATAC donor pseudobulks), sex as the group, three ADNC stages:

motco analyze \
  --block rna=rna_logcpm.csv --block atac=atac_logcpm.csv \
  --metadata donors.csv --sample-col donor_id --group-col Sex --stage-col ADNC \
  --stage-order "Not AD + Low,Intermediate,High" \
  --permutations 999 --seed 20261015 \
  --out-dir results/motco_mtg_astro

For the dimensionality sensitivity analysis, re-run with --forced-components 2, 3, … into separate output directories.

from motco.analysis import (
    OmicsBlock, TrajectoryAnalysisParams, TrajectoryDataset,
    analyze_trajectories, write_analysis_outputs,
)

dataset = TrajectoryDataset(
    blocks=[OmicsBlock("rna", rna), OmicsBlock("atac", atac)],
    metadata=donors,
    sample_col="donor_id", group_col="Sex", stage_col="ADNC",
    stage_order=["Not AD + Low", "Intermediate", "High"],
)
result = analyze_trajectories(dataset, TrajectoryAnalysisParams(permutations=999, seed=20261015))
write_analysis_outputs(result, "results/motco_mtg_astro")

docs.title: motco.analysis
docs.text:
Real-data trajectory analysis: the validated MOTCO measurement on your own data.

:func:analyze_trajectories runs the production pipeline the simulation harness characterizes — pooled per-feature standardization, a stage-supervised PLS-DA latent space whose rank is chosen by double cross-validation, delta / angle / shape between two groups in that space, and RRPP p-values — on caller-supplied omic blocks and sample metadata. It calls the same cores as :func:motco.simulations.evaluate_semisynthetic_trajectory (block scaling in :mod:motco.simulations.preprocessing, :func:~motco.simulations.evaluation.fit_pls_latent_space, the trajectory design and the record helpers), so the measurement exists once.

Two inputs are load-bearing and therefore explicit:

  • Stage order. Net displacement runs from the first to the last declared stage, and shape and the spectrum follow that order. It is never inferred by sorting labels.
  • Units. Each block declares its unit transform (identity or beta_to_mvalue). MOTCO does not normalize counts, filter features or impute values; blocks are analysed in the units supplied.

Declared covariates enter the trajectory model. By default the latent space is built without them; TrajectoryAnalysisParams.covariate_latent_adjustment ("stage" or "group_stage") instead fits the basis on features residualized on the covariates conditional on that design, and measures the raw features in it.

:func:write_analysis_outputs writes the result as plain JSON/CSV (record, latent scores, PLS loadings, latent stage means and, when requested, the attribution tables) — the fitted estimator is never pickled.

docs.title: TrajectoryDataset dataclass
docs.text:
Aligned omic blocks plus sample metadata, validated on construction.

Every block's rows must equal metadata[sample_col] in order. The group column must hold exactly two labels; stage_order must list every observed stage label exactly once (labels are compared as strings), and every group × stage cell must be observed.

covariate_cols names metadata columns that enter the trajectory model additively, in declared order. A covariate is categorical when listed in categorical_covariates or when its dtype is not numeric (booleans are categorical); otherwise numeric. missing_covariates decides what a missing covariate value does: "error" rejects it, "complete_case" drops the sample from the metadata and every block before anything else is validated or fitted (dropped_sample_ids lists them). Covariates are never imputed.

Source code in src/motco/analysis.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TrajectoryDataset:
    """Aligned omic blocks plus sample metadata, validated on construction.

    Every block's rows must equal ``metadata[sample_col]`` in order. The group
    column must hold exactly two labels; ``stage_order`` must list every
    observed stage label exactly once (labels are compared as strings), and
    every group × stage cell must be observed.

    ``covariate_cols`` names metadata columns that enter the trajectory model
    additively, in declared order. A covariate is categorical when listed in
    ``categorical_covariates`` or when its dtype is not numeric (booleans are
    categorical); otherwise numeric. ``missing_covariates`` decides what a
    missing covariate value does: ``"error"`` rejects it, ``"complete_case"``
    drops the sample from the metadata and every block before anything else is
    validated or fitted (``dropped_sample_ids`` lists them). Covariates are
    never imputed.
    """

    blocks: Sequence[OmicsBlock]
    metadata: pd.DataFrame
    sample_col: str
    group_col: str
    stage_col: str
    stage_order: Sequence[str]
    group_order: Sequence[str] | None = None
    covariate_cols: Sequence[str] = ()
    categorical_covariates: Sequence[str] = ()
    missing_covariates: MissingCovariatePolicy = "error"
    _dropped_sample_ids: tuple[str, ...] = field(default=(), init=False, repr=False, compare=False)
    _covariate_design: CovariateDesign | None = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False, compare=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(self, "blocks", tuple(self.blocks))
        object.__setattr__(self, "stage_order", tuple(str(stage) for stage in self.stage_order))
        if self.group_order is not None:
            object.__setattr__(self, "group_order", tuple(str(group) for group in self.group_order))
        object.__setattr__(self, "covariate_cols", tuple(self.covariate_cols))
        object.__setattr__(self, "categorical_covariates", tuple(self.categorical_covariates))
        self._validate_metadata()
        self._validate_covariate_declarations()
        cells_before = self._observed_cells()
        self._apply_missing_covariate_policy()
        self._validate_blocks(self.sample_ids)
        self._build_covariate_design()
        self._validate_design(cells_before)

    @property
    def sample_ids(self) -> list[str]:
        return self.metadata[self.sample_col].astype(str).tolist()

    @property
    def groups(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Group labels in analysis order (declared, else sorted as strings)."""

        if self.group_order is not None:
            return tuple(self.group_order)
        return tuple(sorted(set(self.metadata[self.group_col].astype(str))))

    @property
    def stages(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return tuple(self.stage_order)

    @property
    def dropped_sample_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Samples removed by complete-case deletion (empty under ``"error"``)."""

        return self._dropped_sample_ids

    @property
    def covariate_design(self) -> CovariateDesign | None:
        """The covariate design columns on the retained samples, or ``None`` without covariates."""

        return self._covariate_design

    def _observed_cells(self) -> set[tuple[str, str]]:
        return set(zip(self.metadata[self.group_col].astype(str), self.metadata[self.stage_col].astype(str)))

    def _validate_covariate_declarations(self) -> None:
        if self.missing_covariates not in MISSING_COVARIATE_POLICIES:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Unknown missing_covariates policy {self.missing_covariates!r}; allowed: "
                f"{list(MISSING_COVARIATE_POLICIES)}."
            )
        covariates = list(self.covariate_cols)
        repeated = sorted({name for name in covariates if covariates.count(name) > 1})
        if repeated:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"Covariates must be declared once; repeated: {repeated}.")
        reserved = [name for name in covariates if name in {self.sample_col, self.group_col, self.stage_col}]
        if reserved:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Covariates must differ from the sample, group and stage columns; got {reserved}."
            )
        absent = [name for name in covariates if name not in self.metadata.columns]
        if absent:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"metadata is missing covariate column(s): {absent}.")
        undeclared = [name for name in self.categorical_covariates if name not in covariates]
        if undeclared:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"categorical_covariates must also be declared in covariate_cols; not declared: {undeclared}."
            )

    def _apply_missing_covariate_policy(self) -> None:
        if not self.covariate_cols:
            return
        missing = self.metadata[list(self.covariate_cols)].isna()
        if not missing.to_numpy().any():
            return
        sample_ids = self.metadata[self.sample_col].astype(str)
        if self.missing_covariates == "error":
            column = next(name for name in self.covariate_cols if missing[name].any())
            affected = sample_ids[missing[column].to_numpy()].tolist()
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Covariate {column!r} has missing values for {len(affected)} sample(s): {affected[:10]}. "
                "Pass missing_covariates='complete_case' to drop them; covariates are never imputed."
            )
        drop = missing.any(axis=1).to_numpy()
        keep = ~drop
        object.__setattr__(self, "_dropped_sample_ids", tuple(sample_ids[drop].tolist()))
        object.__setattr__(self, "metadata", self.metadata.loc[keep].reset_index(drop=True))
        retained = []
        for block in self.blocks:
            values = block.values
            if isinstance(values, pd.DataFrame) and values.shape[0] == keep.size:
                values = values.loc[keep]
            retained.append(OmicsBlock(block.name, values, block.transform))
        object.__setattr__(self, "blocks", tuple(retained))

    def _build_covariate_design(self) -> None:
        if not self.covariate_cols:
            return
        try:
            design = build_covariate_matrix(self.metadata, self.covariate_cols, self.categorical_covariates)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(str(exc)) from exc
        object.__setattr__(self, "_covariate_design", design)

    def _validate_metadata(self) -> None:
        if not isinstance(self.metadata, pd.DataFrame):
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("metadata must be a pandas DataFrame.")
        columns = {"sample_col": self.sample_col, "group_col": self.group_col, "stage_col": self.stage_col}
        missing = [f"{role}={name!r}" for role, name in columns.items() if name not in self.metadata.columns]
        if missing:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"metadata is missing column(s): {', '.join(missing)}.")
        if len({self.sample_col, self.group_col, self.stage_col}) != 3:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("sample_col, group_col and stage_col must name three different columns.")
        if self.metadata.shape[0] == 0:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("metadata must contain at least one sample.")
        for name in columns.values():
            if self.metadata[name].isna().any():
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"metadata column {name!r} contains missing values.")
        sample_ids = self.sample_ids
        duplicated = sorted({sid for sid in sample_ids if sample_ids.count(sid) > 1})
        if duplicated:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"metadata sample ids are not unique: {duplicated[:10]}.")

    def _validate_blocks(self, sample_ids: list[str]) -> None:
        if not self.blocks:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("At least one omic block is required.")
        names = [block.name for block in self.blocks]
        repeated = sorted({name for name in names if names.count(name) > 1})
        if repeated:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"Block names must be unique; repeated: {repeated}.")
        for block in self.blocks:
            if not isinstance(block.name, str) or not block.name:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"Block names must be non-empty strings, got {block.name!r}.")
            if block.transform not in UNIT_TRANSFORMS:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"Block {block.name!r} declares unknown transform {block.transform!r}; "
                    f"allowed: {list(UNIT_TRANSFORMS)}."
                )
            values = block.values
            if not isinstance(values, pd.DataFrame):
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"Block {block.name!r} must be a pandas DataFrame.")
            if values.shape[0] != len(sample_ids):
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"Block {block.name!r} has {values.shape[0]} rows but metadata has {len(sample_ids)} samples."
                )
            if values.index.astype(str).tolist() != sample_ids:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"Block {block.name!r} rows are not aligned to metadata column {self.sample_col!r} "
                    "(same sample ids in the same order are required)."
                )
            if values.shape[1] == 0:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"Block {block.name!r} must contain at least one feature.")
            features = values.columns.astype(str).tolist()
            if len(set(features)) != len(features):
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"Block {block.name!r} has duplicate feature names.")
            try:
                matrix = values.to_numpy(dtype=float)
            except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"Block {block.name!r} holds non-numeric values.") from exc
            if not np.all(np.isfinite(matrix)):
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"Block {block.name!r} contains missing or infinite values; complete matrices are "
                    "required and no imputation is performed."
                )
            if block.transform == "beta_to_mvalue" and not np.all((matrix > 0.0) & (matrix < 1.0)):
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"Block {block.name!r} declares beta_to_mvalue but holds values outside the open "
                    "interval (0, 1)."
                )

    def _validate_design(self, cells_before: set[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
        emptied = sorted(cells_before - self._observed_cells())
        if emptied:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Complete-case deletion of {len(self._dropped_sample_ids)} sample(s) with missing covariates "
                f"emptied group/stage combination(s): {emptied}."
            )
        observed_stages = sorted(set(self.metadata[self.stage_col].astype(str)))
        declared = list(self.stage_order)
        if len(set(declared)) != len(declared) or set(declared) != set(observed_stages):
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"stage_order must list every observed stage label exactly once; declared {declared}, "
                f"observed {observed_stages}."
            )
        if len(declared) < 2:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"At least two stages are required; observed {observed_stages}.")
        observed_groups = sorted(set(self.metadata[self.group_col].astype(str)))
        if len(observed_groups) != 2:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Exactly two groups are required in {self.group_col!r}; found {len(observed_groups)}: "
                f"{observed_groups}."
            )
        if self.group_order is not None:
            group_order = list(self.group_order)
            if len(set(group_order)) != len(group_order) or set(group_order) != set(observed_groups):
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                    f"group_order must list both observed groups exactly once; declared {group_order}, "
                    f"observed {observed_groups}."
                )
        present = self._observed_cells()
        missing = [(group, stage) for group in self.groups for stage in declared if (group, stage) not in present]
        if missing:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"metadata has no sample for group/stage combination(s): {missing}.")

docs.title: TrajectoryAnalysisParams dataclass
docs.text:
Measurement settings; the defaults are the simulation harness's.

forced_components fixes the latent rank (dimensionality sensitivity) and skips cross-validation; None selects it by double CV. seed seeds RRPP exactly as the harness does.

covariate_latent_adjustment (None, "stage" or "group_stage") opts into covariate-aware latent construction: the basis is fitted on features residualized on the declared covariates, conditional on the stage or the group × stage indicators. It requires declared covariates and is omitted from :meth:to_dict while None.

min_components is the rank floor of the cross-validated latent space (default 2, so angle and shape are measured in at least two dimensions). 1 restores the unfloored 0.9.0 rule and normalizes to None, which is omitted from :meth:to_dict and from the record's latent block, so a floor-1 analysis reproduces every 0.9.0 artifact. A floor below 1 is rejected before any fitting. The floor guarantees two dimensions, not a second axis with signal.

Source code in src/motco/analysis.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TrajectoryAnalysisParams:
    """Measurement settings; the defaults are the simulation harness's.

    ``forced_components`` fixes the latent rank (dimensionality sensitivity) and
    skips cross-validation; ``None`` selects it by double CV. ``seed`` seeds
    RRPP exactly as the harness does.

    ``covariate_latent_adjustment`` (``None``, ``"stage"`` or
    ``"group_stage"``) opts into covariate-aware latent construction: the
    basis is fitted on features residualized on the declared covariates,
    conditional on the stage or the group × stage indicators. It requires
    declared covariates and is omitted from :meth:`to_dict` while ``None``.

    ``min_components`` is the rank floor of the cross-validated latent space
    (default 2, so ``angle`` and ``shape`` are measured in at least two
    dimensions). ``1`` restores the unfloored 0.9.0 rule and normalizes to
    ``None``, which is omitted from :meth:`to_dict` and from the record's
    ``latent`` block, so a floor-1 analysis reproduces every 0.9.0 artifact.
    A floor below 1 is rejected before any fitting. The floor guarantees two
    dimensions, not a second axis with signal.
    """

    permutations: int = 0
    seed: int | None = None
    n_jobs: int = 1
    orientation_estimator: str = "net_displacement"
    forced_components: int | None = None
    cv1_splits: int = 3
    cv2_splits: int = 4
    n_repeats: int = 5
    max_components: int = 20
    random_state: int = 1203
    attribution: AttributionDiagnosticSettings = field(default_factory=AttributionDiagnosticSettings)
    progress: bool = False
    covariate_latent_adjustment: str | None = None
    min_components: int | None = 2

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        floor = self.min_components
        if floor is not None:
            if isinstance(floor, bool) or not isinstance(floor, (int, np.integer)) or floor < 1:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(f"min_components must be an integer of at least 1, got {floor!r}.")
            # 1 is the unfloored 0.9.0 rule: held as ``None`` so the record stays byte-identical.
            object.__setattr__(self, "min_components", None if int(floor) == 1 else int(floor))
        if self.covariate_latent_adjustment is not None and self.covariate_latent_adjustment not in CONDITIONING_KINDS:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Unknown covariate_latent_adjustment {self.covariate_latent_adjustment!r}; allowed: "
                f"{list(CONDITIONING_KINDS)} or None."
            )
        if self.orientation_estimator not in EVALUATION_ORIENTATION_ESTIMATORS:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
                f"Unknown orientation_estimator {self.orientation_estimator!r}; allowed: "
                f"{list(EVALUATION_ORIENTATION_ESTIMATORS)}."
            )
        if self.permutations < 0:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("permutations must be greater than or equal to 0.")
        if self.n_jobs == 0:
            raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("n_jobs must be -1 or a non-zero integer.")
        settings = self.attribution
        if settings.enabled:
            if settings.bootstrap_replicates < 0:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("attribution.bootstrap_replicates must be greater than or equal to 0.")
            if settings.top_k < 1:
                raise TrajectoryAnalysisError("attribution.top_k must be at least 1.")

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        data = asdict(self)
        if self.covariate_latent_adjustment is None:
            # Absent means the 0.8.0 analysis: its resolved parameters stay byte-identical.
            data.pop("covariate_latent_adjustment")
        if self.min_components is None:
            # Floor 1 means the 0.9.0 rank rule: its resolved parameters stay byte-identical.
            data.pop("min_components")
        return data

    @property
    def resolved_min_components(self) -> int:
        """The rank floor the cross-validation runs with (1 when omitted)."""

        return self.min_components or 1
