docs.text:
Measure two groups' trajectories across ordered stages on real data.

Standardizes every block with pooled per-feature scalers (after its unit transform), concatenates the blocks in declared order as f"{block}__{feature}", builds the stage-supervised PLS-DA latent space (double-CV rank, or params.forced_components), estimates delta, angle (net displacement by default) and shape between the groups in that space and, when params.permutations > 0, their RRPP p-values. Records the selected rank, null summary, stage-mean spectrum, cell sizes, block units and software versions beside the statistics. Optionally runs frozen-model orientation attribution on the fitted estimator.

Declared covariates (dataset.covariate_cols) are appended additively to the full (group × stage) and reduced (group + stage) trajectory models, so RRPP permutes residuals of the reduced model with covariates. Every LS-mean is evaluated at the pooled covariate mean; delta, angle and shape do not depend on that reference. The latent space is fitted without the covariates unless params.covariate_latent_adjustment is set: then the pooled-standardized features are residualized on the covariates conditional on the stage ("stage") or group × stage ("group_stage") indicators before the basis is fitted (per training set inside the cross-validation, at the pooled scale), the raw features are projected onto that basis, and the trajectory model, LS-means and RRPP are unchanged. Attribution is not available with covariates.

def analyze_trajectories(
    dataset: TrajectoryDataset,
    params: TrajectoryAnalysisParams | None = None,
) -> TrajectoryAnalysisResult:
    """Measure two groups' trajectories across ordered stages on real data.

    Standardizes every block with pooled per-feature scalers (after its unit
    transform), concatenates the blocks in declared order as
    ``f"{block}__{feature}"``, builds the stage-supervised PLS-DA latent space
    (double-CV rank, or ``params.forced_components``), estimates ``delta``,
    ``angle`` (net displacement by default) and ``shape`` between the groups
    in that space and, when ``params.permutations > 0``, their RRPP p-values.
    Records the selected rank, null summary, stage-mean spectrum, cell sizes,
    block units and software versions beside the statistics. Optionally runs
    frozen-model orientation attribution on the fitted estimator.

    Declared covariates (``dataset.covariate_cols``) are appended additively to
    the full (group × stage) and reduced (group + stage) trajectory models, so
    RRPP permutes residuals of the reduced model with covariates. Every LS-mean
    is evaluated at the pooled covariate mean; ``delta``, ``angle`` and
    ``shape`` do not depend on that reference. The latent space is fitted
    without the covariates unless ``params.covariate_latent_adjustment`` is
    set: then the pooled-standardized features are residualized on the
    covariates conditional on the stage (``"stage"``) or group × stage
    (``"group_stage"``) indicators before the basis is fitted (per training set
    inside the cross-validation, at the pooled scale), the raw features are
    projected onto that basis, and the trajectory model, LS-means and RRPP are
    unchanged. Attribution is not available with covariates.
    """

    params = params or TrajectoryAnalysisParams()
    covariates = dataset.covariate_design
    if params.covariate_latent_adjustment is not None and covariates is None:
        raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
            f"Latent adjustment ({params.covariate_latent_adjustment!r}) requires declared covariates; "
            "declare covariate_cols on the dataset or drop the setting."
        )
    if covariates is not None and params.attribution.enabled:
        raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
            "Attribution is not available with covariates: it works from unadjusted cell means. "
            "Disable attribution or drop the covariates."
        )
    start = perf_counter()
    blocks = {block.name: block.values for block in dataset.blocks}
    order = [block.name for block in dataset.blocks]
    transforms = {block.name: block.transform for block in dataset.blocks}

    scalers = fit_block_scalers(blocks, transforms)
    standardized = transform_blocks(blocks, scalers, transforms)
    X = concatenate_blocks(standardized, order).reset_index(drop=True)

    groups = list(dataset.groups)
    stages = list(dataset.stages)
    group_codes = {label: str(index) for index, label in enumerate(groups)}
    stage_codes = {label: str(index) for index, label in enumerate(stages)}
    working = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            _GROUP: dataset.metadata[dataset.group_col].astype(str).map(group_codes).to_numpy(),
            _STAGE: dataset.metadata[dataset.stage_col].astype(str).map(stage_codes).to_numpy(),
        }
    )

    integration_params: dict[str, Any] = {
        "cv1_splits": params.cv1_splits,
        "cv2_splits": params.cv2_splits,
        "n_repeats": params.n_repeats,
        "max_components": params.max_components,
        "random_state": params.random_state,
        "n_jobs": params.n_jobs,
    }
    if params.forced_components is not None:
        integration_params["forced_components"] = params.forced_components
    nuisance = _latent_nuisance(working, covariates, params.covariate_latent_adjustment)
    sample_ids = dataset.sample_ids
    try:
        latent = fit_pls_latent_space(
            X,
            working[_STAGE],
            integration_params,
            stage_col=dataset.stage_col,
            sample_ids=sample_ids,
            layer_feature_counts={name: int(frame.shape[1]) for name, frame in blocks.items()},
            layers_metadata={},
            original_scales=_joint_original_scales(scalers, order, X.columns),
            methylation_units=_methylation_units(transforms),
            nuisance=nuisance,
            min_components=params.resolved_min_components,
        )
        design = build_simulation_trajectory_design(working, group_col=_GROUP, stage_col=_STAGE)
    except SimulationEvaluationError as exc:
        raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(str(exc)) from exc
    group_levels = [groups[int(code)] for code in design.group_levels]
    stage_levels = [stages[int(code)] for code in design.stage_levels]
    if stage_levels != stages or group_levels != groups:
        raise TrajectoryAnalysisError(
            f"Internal level mapping mismatch: design levels {group_levels}/{stage_levels}, "
            f"declared {groups}/{stages}."
        )
    model_full, model_reduced, ls_means = _covariate_adjusted_design(
        design.model_full, design.model_reduced, design.ls_means, covariates
    )

    observed_deltas, observed_angles, observed_shapes, observed_spectra = estimate_difference(
        Y=latent.matrix,
        model_matrix=model_full,
        LS_means=ls_means,
        contrast=design.contrast,
        return_spectra=True,
        orientation_estimator=params.orientation_estimator,
    )
    config_spectrum = _config_spectrum_block(observed_spectra, group_levels)
    shape_available = len(stage_levels) >= 3
    pair_statistics = _extract_pair_statistics(
        observed_deltas, observed_angles, observed_shapes, shape_available=shape_available
    )

    p_values: dict[str, float] = {}
    null_summary: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
    if params.permutations > 0:
        dist_delta, dist_angle, dist_shape, dist_eigengap = RRPP(
            latent.matrix,
            model_full,
            model_reduced,
            ls_means,
            design.contrast,
            permutations=params.permutations,
            n_jobs=params.n_jobs,
            progress=params.progress,
            seed=params.seed,
            return_eigengaps=True,
            orientation_estimator=params.orientation_estimator,
        )
        null_values = _extract_null_distributions(
            dist_delta, dist_angle, dist_shape, shape_available=shape_available
        )
        p_values = {
            statistic: _empirical_p_value(null_values[statistic], observed)
            for statistic, observed in pair_statistics.items()
            if statistic in null_values and np.isfinite(observed)
        }
        null_summary = _summarize_null_distributions(null_values)
        config_spectrum["permutation_pooled_eigengap"] = _summarize_permutation_eigengaps(dist_eigengap)

    latent_scores = latent.matrix.copy()
    latent_scores.index.name = dataset.sample_col
    artifacts = latent.artifacts
    assert artifacts is not None  # the PLS core always returns its fitted artifacts
    pls_loadings = _loadings_frame(artifacts.model, X.columns, list(latent.matrix.columns))
    betas = np.asarray(estimate_betas(model_full, latent.matrix.to_numpy(dtype=float)), dtype=float)
    stage_means = _stage_means_frame(
        ls_means,
        betas,
        group_levels,
        stage_levels,
        list(latent.matrix.columns),
    )

    attribution_record, attribution_result = _run_attribution(dataset, params, latent, X, transforms)
    cell_sizes = {
        group: {
            stage: int(
                (
                    (dataset.metadata[dataset.group_col].astype(str) == group)
                    & (dataset.metadata[dataset.stage_col].astype(str) == stage)
                ).sum()
            )
            for stage in stage_levels
        }
        for group in group_levels
    }
    record: dict[str, Any] = {
        "schema_version": ANALYSIS_SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "statistics": pair_statistics,
        "p_values": p_values,
        "null_summary": null_summary,
        "config_spectrum": config_spectrum,
        "latent": latent.metadata,
        "design": {
            "group_col": dataset.group_col,
            "stage_col": dataset.stage_col,
            "sample_col": dataset.sample_col,
            "group_levels": group_levels,
            "stage_levels": stage_levels,
            "cell_sizes": cell_sizes,
            "contrast": design.contrast,
            "n_samples": len(sample_ids),
        },
        **(
            {"covariates": _covariate_record(dataset, covariates, betas, list(latent.matrix.columns))}
            if covariates is not None
            else {}
        ),
        **(
            {"latent_adjustment": _latent_adjustment_record(dataset, artifacts.latent_adjustment)}
            if artifacts.latent_adjustment is not None
            else {}
        ),
        "blocks": [
            {
                "name": block.name,
                "n_features": int(block.values.shape[1]),
                "transform": block.transform,
                "units": _TRANSFORM_UNITS[block.transform],
            }
            for block in dataset.blocks
        ],
        "measurement": {
            "orientation_estimator": params.orientation_estimator,
            "selected_lv": latent.metadata["selected_lv"],
            "component_selection": latent.metadata["component_selection"],
            "permutations": params.permutations,
            "seed": params.seed,
            "n_jobs": params.n_jobs,
            "shape_available": shape_available,
            "runtime_seconds": perf_counter() - start,
        },
        "params": params.to_dict(),
        "software": _software_versions(),
        "attribution": attribution_record,
    }
    return TrajectoryAnalysisResult(
        record=_json_safe(record),
        latent_scores=latent_scores,
        pls_loadings=pls_loadings,
        stage_means=stage_means,
        attribution=attribution_result,
    )

def write_analysis_outputs(
    result: TrajectoryAnalysisResult,
    out_dir: str | Path,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
) -> dict[str, Path]:
    """Write the analysis artifact to ``out_dir`` and return the written paths.

    Writes ``result.json``, ``latent_scores.csv``, ``pls_loadings.csv``,
    ``stage_means.csv`` and, when attribution ran, its tables under
    ``attribution/``. Refuses to touch a directory that already holds
    ``result.json`` unless ``overwrite`` is set.
    """

    directory = Path(out_dir)
    result_path = directory / "result.json"
    if result_path.exists() and not overwrite:
        raise FileExistsError(f"{result_path} already exists; pass overwrite=True to replace the analysis.")
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    paths: dict[str, Path] = {}
    result_path.write_text(json.dumps(result.record, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    paths["result"] = result_path
    paths["latent_scores"] = directory / "latent_scores.csv"
    result.latent_scores.to_csv(paths["latent_scores"])
    paths["pls_loadings"] = directory / "pls_loadings.csv"
    result.pls_loadings.to_csv(paths["pls_loadings"], index=False)
    paths["stage_means"] = directory / "stage_means.csv"
    result.stage_means.to_csv(paths["stage_means"], index=False)
    if result.attribution is not None:
        for name, path in write_attribution_outputs(result.attribution, directory / "attribution").items():
            paths[f"attribution/{name}"] = path
    return paths

docs.title: Orientation Driver Attribution
docs.text:
Orientation attribution explains a two-group, multi-stage difference after an upstream trajectory analysis has identified the shared PLS space of interest. Pass the pooled, aligned feature matrix, matching group/stage metadata, and the one fitted PLS estimator to analyze_orientation_attribution.

The analysis orders groups and stages deterministically unless explicit levels are supplied. For every adjacent stage pair it reports each group's raw transition and path length, the unit directional contrast, the same contrast after PLS score projection and inverse transformation, and the signed residual observed - pls_captured. Observed feature values remain in the result; the reconstruction is a parallel, lossy view rather than a replacement.

docs.title: Two decompositions
docs.text:
Attribution reports two decompositions, and they explain different quantities.

The principal-orientation block decomposes the tested angle estimand: principal-axis divergence, the contrast between the groups' signed leading principal axes. It applies the same functional the statistic is built from (motco.stats.trajectory.principal_orientation) to each group's stage-mean configuration, observed and PLS-reconstructed, so the explanation and the test cannot drift apart.

The per-adjacent-transition blocks describe where along the trajectory the groups' step directions diverge. They are a per-step description, not the tested estimand; the two decompositions coincide only for a two-stage design, where the configuration is rank one and PC1 is the transition direction.

Both appear in the tabular outputs under the transition_id column — the transitions as from->to, the principal block under principal_component_id (default principal), which is validated against the stage-derived identifiers so the two can never collide.

docs.title: Degeneracy and availability
docs.text:
A principal axis exists for any configuration with variance, but it is only resolvable when one axis dominates. The result reports each contributing configuration's relative eigengap and flags the principal contrast degenerate when any falls below eigengap_threshold (default 0.05). The flagged contrast is still returned: degeneracy is a property of the data, so callers stratify on the flag rather than lose rows.

That is distinct from unavailability. A trajectory whose net displacement from first stage to last is at or below zero_tolerance is closed, and no direction is defined at all — that group's principal orientation is marked unavailable, exactly as a zero-length transition is.

docs.title: Units and stability
docs.text:
Effects are reported in the input coordinate units, normally pooled standardized units. Positive per-feature scales can be supplied to add original-unit columns. These scales only convert reported effects; they never change PLS geometry.

Bootstrap resampling is independent within every group-by-stage cell and uses the same fitted model and preprocessing contract in every replicate. The result records the seed, requested count, valid count, sign stability, and top-k selection frequency, for the principal-orientation block as well as the transitions. Each replicate's principal axis is signed by that replicate's own net displacement, so resampling noise cannot flip the axis; a replicate whose trajectory closes contributes no contrast and counts as invalid. Bootstrap is available for arithmetic row-derived means; precomputed covariate-adjusted mean tables are accepted with stability marked unavailable.

docs.title: Labels and interpretation
docs.text:
Feature-to-module or feature-to-pathway labels are optional and must be a complete one-to-one mapping supplied by the caller. Aggregate tables preserve the labels and mark their source as caller-supplied. Aggregation is not a pathway annotation service and does not establish biological causality.

The result contains no p-values or significance decisions. Attribution should be run after the calling workflow has made any global orientation inference decision. It describes associations implied by one frozen shared PLS model; the inverse reconstruction is not unique, and bootstrap stability is conditional on that fitted representation.

def analyze_orientation_attribution(
    X: pd.DataFrame,
    metadata: pd.DataFrame,
    model: Any,
    *,
    group_col: str = "group",
    stage_col: str = "stage",
    feature_cols: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    groups: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    stages: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    mean_table: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    precomputed_means: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    original_scales: Sequence[float] | pd.Series | Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    feature_scales: Sequence[float] | pd.Series | Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    feature_groups: Mapping[str, str] | pd.Series | pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    group_labels: Mapping[str, str] | pd.Series | pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    label_namespace: str = "module",
    bootstrap_replicates: int = 0,
    bootstrap_seed: int | None = 0,
    top_k: int = 10,
    zero_tolerance: float = 1e-12,
    eigengap_threshold: float = 0.05,
    principal_component_id: str = "principal",
    sample_id_col: str | None = None,
) -> OrientationAttributionResult:
    """Attribute two-group trajectory orientation differences.

    Reports both decompositions described in the module docstring: the
    principal-orientation contrast, which decomposes the tested ``angle``
    estimand and carries a relative-eigengap degeneracy qualifier, and the
    per-adjacent-transition contrasts, which describe where along the trajectory
    the group directions diverge. The two coincide only for a two-stage design.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X:
        Aligned feature matrix in the exact coordinate system consumed by
        ``model``. Observed values are never overwritten by reconstructions.
    metadata:
        Row-aligned metadata containing ``group_col`` and ``stage_col``.
    model:
        One already fitted pooled PLS estimator exposing ``transform`` and
        ``inverse_transform``. It is reused for all groups and replicates.
    mean_table, precomputed_means:
        Optional complete group-by-stage table. It may have a two-level
        MultiIndex or explicit group/stage columns. When supplied, bootstrap
        resampling is unavailable because row-level sampling semantics are not
        defined for adjusted means.
    original_scales, feature_scales:
        Optional positive per-feature scale in canonical feature order. The
        aliases are accepted for readability at call sites; supplying both is
        an error.
    feature_groups, group_labels:
        Optional one-to-one caller-supplied feature-to-label mapping. The
        aliases are accepted for readability at call sites.
    eigengap_threshold:
        Relative-eigengap level at or above which a stage-mean configuration is
        treated as having a well-separated principal axis. A contributing
        configuration below it flags the principal-orientation contrast as
        degenerate; the contrast is still returned, so callers stratify rather
        than lose rows. The default (0.05) separates the audit's resolvable
        replicates from its near-isotropic independent-baseline draws.
    principal_component_id:
        Reserved identifier carrying the principal-orientation component in the
        tabular outputs' ``transition_id`` column. It is validated against the
        stage-derived transition ids so the two can never collide.

    Returns
    -------
    OrientationAttributionResult
        Frozen typed records and DataFrame views for means, transitions, the
        principal-orientation block, feature effects, aggregates, and bootstrap
        stability.
    """
    if mean_table is not None and precomputed_means is not None:
        raise AttributionError("Provide only one of mean_table and precomputed_means.")
    if original_scales is not None and feature_scales is not None:
        raise AttributionError("Provide only one of original_scales and feature_scales.")
    if feature_groups is not None and group_labels is not None:
        raise AttributionError("Provide only one of feature_groups and group_labels.")
    if not isinstance(label_namespace, str) or not label_namespace.strip():
        raise AttributionError("label_namespace must be a non-empty string.")
    if precomputed_means is not None:
        mean_table = precomputed_means
    if feature_scales is not None:
        original_scales = feature_scales
    if group_labels is not None:
        feature_groups = group_labels

    feature_frame, metadata_frame, feature_names = _validate_inputs(
        X,
        metadata,
        model,
        group_col,
        stage_col,
        feature_cols,
        sample_id_col,
    )
    ordered_groups = cast(
        tuple[str, str], _ordered_levels(metadata_frame[group_col], groups, 2, "groups")
    )
    ordered_stages = _ordered_levels(metadata_frame[stage_col], stages, 2, "stages")
    _validate_cells(metadata_frame, group_col, stage_col, ordered_groups, ordered_stages)
    scale_values = _validate_scales(original_scales, feature_names)
    label_values = _validate_feature_groups(feature_groups, feature_names)

    if mean_table is None:
        means_array = _arithmetic_means(
            feature_frame,
            metadata_frame,
            group_col,
            stage_col,
            ordered_groups,
            ordered_stages,
        )
        mean_source = "arithmetic"
    else:
        means_array = _precomputed_mean_array(
            mean_table,
            feature_names,
            ordered_groups,
            ordered_stages,
            group_col,
            stage_col,
        )
        mean_source = "precomputed"
        if bootstrap_replicates:
            raise AttributionError(
                "bootstrap_replicates must be zero when mean_table contains precomputed means; "
                "row-level bootstrap semantics are unavailable."
            )

    _validate_bootstrap_settings(bootstrap_replicates, top_k, zero_tolerance)
    _validate_principal_settings(eigengap_threshold, principal_component_id, ordered_stages)
    reconstructed_array = _reconstruct_means(means_array, model, feature_names)
    transitions = _build_transitions(
        means_array,
        reconstructed_array,
        ordered_groups,
        ordered_stages,
        zero_tolerance,
    )
    principal = _build_principal_orientation(
        means_array,
        reconstructed_array,
        ordered_groups,
        ordered_stages,
        zero_tolerance,
        eigengap_threshold,
        principal_component_id,
    )
    model_components = _model_components(model)
    config = AttributionConfig(
        group_column=group_col,
        stage_column=stage_col,
        feature_names=feature_names,
        groups=ordered_groups,
        stages=ordered_stages,
        mean_source=mean_source,
        input_units="standardized_input",
        original_units_available=scale_values is not None,
        zero_tolerance=float(zero_tolerance),
        bootstrap_replicates=int(bootstrap_replicates),
        bootstrap_seed=bootstrap_seed,
        top_k=int(top_k),
        model_components=model_components,
        label_namespace=label_namespace if label_values is not None else None,
        label_source="caller-supplied" if label_values is not None else None,
        eigengap_threshold=float(eigengap_threshold),
        principal_component_id=principal_component_id,
    )

    bootstrap_records = _bootstrap(
        feature_frame,
        metadata_frame,
        group_col,
        stage_col,
        ordered_groups,
        ordered_stages,
        model,
        feature_names,
        scale_values,
        bootstrap_replicates,
        bootstrap_seed,
        top_k,
        zero_tolerance,
        principal_component_id,
    )
    bootstrap_lookup = {
        (record.transition_id, record.component): record for record in bootstrap_records
    }
    feature_effects, feature_records = _feature_effect_table(
        transitions,
        principal,
        feature_names,
        scale_values,
        bootstrap_lookup,
        label_values,
        label_namespace,
        bootstrap_replicates,
    )
    aggregate_effects, aggregate_records = _aggregate_effect_table(
        feature_effects,
        feature_names,
        label_values,
        label_namespace,
        bootstrap_replicates,
    )
    transition_summaries, transition_vectors = _transition_tables(
        transitions,
        ordered_groups,
        feature_names,
    )
    principal_summaries, principal_vectors = _principal_tables(
        principal,
        ordered_groups,
        feature_names,
    )
    bootstrap_table = _bootstrap_table(bootstrap_records, feature_names)
    means_table = _means_table(means_array, ordered_groups, ordered_stages, feature_names)
    reconstructed_table = _means_table(
        reconstructed_array, ordered_groups, ordered_stages, feature_names
    )
    interpretation = InterpretationMetadata(
        statement="Attribution describes associations implied by one fitted shared PLS representation.",
        causal_boundary="Feature, module, and pathway effects are not causal claims.",
        significance_boundary=(
            "No p-values or significance decisions are produced; external orientation inference remains the caller's "
            "responsibility."
        ),
        reconstruction_boundary=(
            "PLS-captured effects are a lossy inverse-transform view and are not a unique inverse of measured features."
        ),
        bootstrap_boundary=(
            "Bootstrap stability is conditional on the fitted preprocessing contract and frozen PLS model."
        ),
        label_source="caller-supplied" if label_values is not None else None,
        decomposition_boundary=(
            f"The '{principal_component_id}' component decomposes the tested angle estimand — principal-axis "
            "divergence between the groups' signed leading principal axes — while per-adjacent-transition "
            "contrasts describe where along the trajectory the group directions diverge; the two coincide only "
            "for two-stage designs. A degenerate principal contrast is reported with its flag and MUST NOT be "
            "read as a well-defined orientation."
        ),
    )
    return OrientationAttributionResult(
        config=config,
        means=means_table,
        reconstructed_means=reconstructed_table,
        transitions=tuple(transitions),
        principal_orientation=principal,
        feature_effects=feature_effects,
        transition_summaries=transition_summaries,
        transition_vectors=transition_vectors,
        principal_summaries=principal_summaries,
        principal_vectors=principal_vectors,
        aggregate_effects=aggregate_effects,
        bootstrap_summaries=bootstrap_table,
        interpretation=interpretation,
        feature_records=tuple(feature_records),
        aggregate_records=tuple(aggregate_records),
        bootstrap_records=tuple(bootstrap_records),
    )

def attribution_frames(result: OrientationAttributionResult) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return all findings-ready tables for ``result``."""

    configuration = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            ("group_column", result.config.group_column),

            ("stages", list(result.config.stages)),

            ("input_units", result.config.input_units),
            ("original_units_available", result.config.original_units_available),
            ("zero_tolerance", result.config.zero_tolerance),
            ("bootstrap_replicates", result.config.bootstrap_replicates),
            ("bootstrap_seed", result.config.bootstrap_seed),
            ("top_k", result.config.top_k),
            ("model_components", result.config.model_components),
            ("label_namespace", result.config.label_namespace),
            ("label_source", result.config.label_source),
            ("eigengap_threshold", result.config.eigengap_threshold),
            ("principal_component_id", result.config.principal_component_id),
        ],

def write_attribution_outputs(
    result: OrientationAttributionResult,
    output_dir: str | Path,
) -> dict[str, Path]:
    """Write attribution tables as CSV files and return their paths."""

    directory = Path(output_dir)
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    paths: dict[str, Path] = {}
    for name, frame in attribution_frames(result).items():
        path = directory / f"{name}.csv"
        frame.to_csv(path, index=False)
        paths[name] = path
    return paths

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
The motco command-line interface provides five subcommands.

usage: motco [-h] [--version] [--verbose] {plsr,snf,simulate,de,analyze} ...

MOTCO CLI: PLSR, SNF, group differences, and real-data trajectory analysis

positional arguments:
  {plsr,snf,simulate,de,analyze}
    plsr                Run PLS-DA with double cross-validation
    snf                 Similarity Network Fusion
    simulate            Generate a semi-synthetic multi-omics toy dataset (numpy generator, no R)
    de                  Group differences on trajectories (estimate or RRPP)
    analyze             Real-data trajectory analysis with the validated pipeline (PLS latent space, RRPP)

For real data, use motco analyze. It runs the measurement the simulation studies validated, in one step. plsr and de are lower-level building blocks.

docs.title: motco plsr
docs.text:
Run PLS-DA with double cross-validation. Input can be a single CSV (with --data and --label-col) or separate predictor/label CSVs (--x / --y).

usage: motco plsr [-h] [--data DATA] [--label-col LABEL_COL] [--x X] [--y Y]
                  [--cv1-splits CV1_SPLITS] [--cv2-splits CV2_SPLITS]
                  [--n-repeats N_REPEATS] [--max-components MAX_COMPONENTS]
                  [--min-components MIN_COMPONENTS]
                  [--random-state RANDOM_STATE] [--out-table OUT_TABLE]
                  [--out-vips OUT_VIPS]

options:
  --data DATA                CSV with predictors and label column
  --label-col LABEL_COL      Label column name when using --data
  --x X                      CSV with predictors (features)
  --y Y                      CSV with labels/outcomes
  --cv1-splits CV1_SPLITS    Inner CV folds
  --cv2-splits CV2_SPLITS    Outer CV folds
  --n-repeats N_REPEATS      Number of outer CV repeats
  --max-components MAX_COMPONENTS
                             Maximum latent variables to search
  --min-components MIN_COMPONENTS
                             Smallest number of latent variables CV considers; the
                             candidates are MIN..MAX-1 (default: 1, the unfloored rule).
                             A value below 1 or not below --max-components exits
                             non-zero naming both values
  --random-state RANDOM_STATE
                             Random seed for reproducibility
  --out-table OUT_TABLE      Path to save the best models table (CSV)
  --out-vips OUT_VIPS        Path to save VIP scores per feature (CSV)

Example:

motco plsr \
  --data data.csv --label-col group \
  --cv1-splits 5 --cv2-splits 5 --n-repeats 10 --max-components 5 \
  --out-table results/plsr_table.csv \
  --out-vips results/vips.csv

docs.title: motco de
docs.text:
Estimate group trajectory differences, optionally with RRPP permutation testing.

Estimate only (no p-values): provide --model-matrix.

RRPP (with p-values): provide --model-full, --model-reduced, and --rrpp-permutations.

usage: motco de [-h] --Y Y --ls-means LS_MEANS --contrast CONTRAST
                [--model-matrix MODEL_MATRIX] [--model-full MODEL_FULL]
                [--model-reduced MODEL_REDUCED]
                [--rrpp-permutations RRPP_PERMUTATIONS] [--out-json OUT_JSON]
                [--out-observed OUT_OBSERVED]
                [--orientation-estimator {pc1,net_displacement}]

options:
  --Y Y                      Outcome matrix CSV (latent space coordinates)
  --ls-means LS_MEANS        Least-squares means CSV
  --contrast CONTRAST        JSON file with groups (list of index lists)
  --model-matrix MODEL_MATRIX
                             Model matrix CSV (with intercept) for estimate_difference
  --model-full MODEL_FULL    Full model matrix CSV (with intercept) for RRPP
  --model-reduced MODEL_REDUCED
                             Reduced model matrix CSV (with intercept) for RRPP
  --rrpp-permutations RRPP_PERMUTATIONS
                             Number of permutations for RRPP
  --out-json OUT_JSON        Output JSON file
  --out-observed OUT_OBSERVED
                             Save predicted LS-mean vectors as CSV
  --orientation-estimator {pc1,net_displacement}
                             Orientation estimator for angles (default: pc1)

--orientation-estimator selects how each group's orientation is measured, for the observed angles and for every RRPP permutation. The default stays pc1, so existing invocations produce the same output. When the flag is omitted, the JSON is unchanged and has no orientation_estimator key. net_displacement is the estimator the simulation harness and the published operating characteristics describe. When the flag is given, with either value, the JSON records it as "orientation_estimator". Only angles depend on it.

Example — estimate only:

motco de \
  --Y latent.csv --model-matrix model_full.csv \
  --ls-means ls_means.csv --contrast contrast.json \
  --out-json results/de.json \
  --out-observed results/ls_mean_vectors.csv

Example — RRPP:

motco de \
  --Y latent.csv \
  --model-full model_full.csv --model-reduced model_reduced.csv \
  --ls-means ls_means.csv --contrast contrast.json \
  --rrpp-permutations 999 \
  --out-json results/rrpp.json

docs.title: motco analyze
docs.text:
Real-data trajectory analysis with the validated pipeline. See Real-Data Analysis for the input contract, the record and the artifact layout.

usage: motco analyze [-h] --block NAME=PATH [--transform NAME=KIND] --metadata
                     METADATA --sample-col SAMPLE_COL --group-col GROUP_COL
                     --stage-col STAGE_COL [--stage-order STAGE_ORDER]
                     [--group-order GROUP_ORDER] [--covariate COL]
                     [--categorical-covariate COL]
                     [--missing-covariates {error,complete_case}]
                     [--latent-adjustment {stage,group_stage}]
                     [--permutations PERMUTATIONS]
                     [--seed SEED] [--n-jobs N_JOBS]
                     [--forced-components FORCED_COMPONENTS]
                     [--min-components MIN_COMPONENTS]
                     [--orientation-estimator {net_displacement,pc1}]
                     [--attribution]
                     [--bootstrap-replicates BOOTSTRAP_REPLICATES]
                     [--bootstrap-seed BOOTSTRAP_SEED] [--top-k TOP_K]
                     [--cv1-splits CV1_SPLITS] [--cv2-splits CV2_SPLITS]
                     [--n-repeats N_REPEATS] [--max-components MAX_COMPONENTS]
                     [--cv-random-state CV_RANDOM_STATE] --out-dir OUT_DIR
                     [--overwrite]

options:
  --block NAME=PATH          Omic block CSV (samples x features, first column the sample id);
                             repeat per block, in joint feature order
  --transform NAME=KIND      Unit transform for a declared block: identity (default) or beta_to_mvalue
  --metadata METADATA        Sample metadata CSV
  --sample-col, --group-col, --stage-col
                             Metadata columns: sample ids, the two groups, the stages
  --stage-order STAGE_ORDER  Required. Comma-separated stage labels, first to last
  --group-order GROUP_ORDER  Comma-separated group labels (default: sorted as strings)
  --covariate COL            Metadata column entering the trajectory model additively; repeat per
                             covariate, in model order (non-numeric columns are categorical)
  --categorical-covariate COL
                             Like --covariate, but treat the column as a factor whatever its dtype
  --missing-covariates {error,complete_case}
                             Missing covariate values: error (default) or complete_case (drop those
                             samples); never imputed
  --latent-adjustment {stage,group_stage}
                             Fit the PLS basis on features residualized on the declared covariates,
                             conditional on the stage (stage) or group x stage (group_stage)
                             indicators; requires a covariate. Default: off (covariate-blind basis)
  --permutations N           RRPP permutations (default: 0, no p-values)
  --seed SEED                RRPP seed
  --n-jobs N_JOBS            Parallel jobs for CV and RRPP (-1 = all CPUs)
  --forced-components K      Fix the latent rank and skip cross-validation
  --min-components N         Rank floor of the cross-validated latent space: CV considers
                             ranks N..MAX-1 (default: 2; 1 restores the unfloored 0.9.0 rule);
                             a value below 1 exits non-zero
  --orientation-estimator {net_displacement,pc1}
                             Orientation estimator (default: net_displacement)
  --attribution              Run frozen-model orientation attribution
  --bootstrap-replicates, --bootstrap-seed, --top-k
                             Attribution bootstrap settings
  --cv1-splits 3, --cv2-splits 4, --n-repeats 5, --max-components 20, --cv-random-state 1203
                             Cross-validation settings (harness defaults)
  --out-dir OUT_DIR          Directory for the analysis artifact
  --overwrite                Replace an existing analysis in --out-dir

Blocks are analysed in the units supplied: MOTCO does not normalize counts, filter features or impute values. On success the command prints the selected rank with its floor, the estimator, the statistics with their p-values and the written paths; with covariates it also prints each covariate's kind and the number of samples complete-case deletion dropped, and with --latent-adjustment the conditioning and the residual degrees of freedom of the residualization. Covariates are declared in flag order across --covariate and --categorical-covariate. --latent-adjustment without a covariate flag exits non-zero before any data are read; see Latent adjustment for what it changes and the mediator caveat. Input and validation errors exit non-zero with an Error: … message.

Example:

motco analyze \
  --block rna=rna_logcpm.csv --block atac=atac_logcpm.csv \
  --metadata donors.csv --sample-col donor_id --group-col Sex --stage-col ADNC \
  --stage-order "Not AD + Low,Intermediate,High" \
  --permutations 999 --seed 20261015 \
  --out-dir results/motco_mtg_astro

docs.title: PLS-DA
docs.text: Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis with double cross-validation.

docs.title: Scale and nuisance residualization
docs.text:
plsda_doubleCV takes four keyword-only arguments whose defaults reproduce its earlier behaviour exactly:

  • scale (default True) is passed to every PLSRegression fit in the inner loop, the outer loop and the per-repeat refits. False fits in the metric the predictors are already in, for example pooled-standardized features that must keep their pooled scale.
  • nuisance (default None) takes a NuisanceDesign: row-aligned conditioning columns D (no intercept) and covariate columns C. Every training set (each outer rest set and each inner training set) regresses its predictors on [1, D, C], subtracts the fitted covariate part C γ, and residualizes its held-out rows as X_held_out − C_held_out γ. The held-out rows' conditioning (their labels) is never read. The per-repeat refits use coefficients estimated on all rows. Every training design must have full column rank, or the function raises a ValueError naming the repeat and fold, for example when a factor level is absent from a training set. The result gains "nuisance_min_training_df", the smallest training-set residual degrees of freedom.
  • strata (default None) names row-aligned labels both CV levels stratify on instead of y; the AUROC still scores y. Folds depend only on the partition the labels define, so labels that partition the rows like y reproduce the default folds. With a nuisance design, pass nuisance.cells() (its conditioning cells) so every training set contains every cell: the inner folds are not shuffled, and on rows sorted by group within stage a stage-only stratification can put a whole group × stage cell into one validation fold.
  • min_components (default 1) is the smallest number of latent variables the inner CV considers: the candidates are min_components … max_components − 1, so every outer-fold selection, every modal LV in the table and every refit model has at least that many components. It must satisfy 1 ≤ min_components < max_components, or the function raises a ValueError naming both values before any fold is fitted. The default is the unfloored rule; the trajectory latent space (fit_pls_latent_space, shared by the simulation harness and motco analyze) applies a floor of 2 by default, see Real-data analysis.

The real-data analysis uses scale, nuisance and strata together for covariate-aware latent construction; see Real-data analysis.

docs.title: motco.stats.pls.plsda_doubleCV(X, y, cv1_splits=7, cv2_splits=8, n_repeats=30, max_components=50, random_state=1203, n_jobs=1, progress=True, *, scale=True, nuisance=None, strata=None, min_components=1)
docs.text:
Run canonical double-nested cross-validation for PLS-DA.

For each outer fold, the inner CV averages AUROC across its V folds and selects the n_LV with the highest mean. The outer fold's selected n_LV is then evaluated on its held-out test set. Per repeat, the K outer-fold test AUROCs are aggregated by mean (and sample std), and the per-fold n_LV choices are aggregated by mode (parsimony tie-break). One final model is refit per repeat on the full input using the modal n_LV.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default X DataFrame

The predictor variables.

required y Union[DataFrame, Series]

The outcome variable.

required cv1_splits int

Number of folds in the CV1 (inner) loop. Default: 7.

7 cv2_splits int

Number of folds in the CV2 (outer) loop. Default: 8.

8 n_repeats int

Number of repeats of the K-fold outer CV. Default: 30.

30 max_components int

Maximum number of LV to test (candidates are min_components..max_components-1). Default: 50.

50 random_state int

For reproducibility. Default: 1203.

1203 n_jobs int

Number of parallel workers for the inner CV loop. Use -1 for all available CPUs. Default: 1 (serial).

1 progress bool

Whether to display a tqdm progress bar over outer folds. Default: True.

True scale bool

Keyword-only. Whether every PLS fit (inner, outer and the per-repeat refits) rescales the predictors to unit variance. False fits in the metric X is already in. Default: True.

True nuisance NuisanceDesign | None

Keyword-only. When given (row-aligned to X), every training set — each outer rest set and each inner training set — estimates the covariate coefficients of X on [1, conditioning, covariates] from its own rows (:func:fit_nuisance_coefficients), residualizes its own rows, and residualizes the held-out rows with the same coefficients and the held-out covariate columns alone, so held-out labels never enter the residualization. The per-repeat refits use coefficients estimated on all rows. Every training design must have full column rank; otherwise a ValueError names the repeat and fold. Default: None (no residualization).

None strata Union[ndarray, Series, Sequence[str], None]

Keyword-only. Row-aligned labels the outer and inner folds are stratified on instead of y (for example the conditioning cells of nuisance, so that every training set contains every cell). Folds depend only on the partition the labels define, so labels that partition the rows like y reproduce the default folds. Default: None (stratify on y).

None min_components int

Keyword-only. The smallest number of latent variables the inner CV considers, so the candidates are min_components..max_components-1 and every outer-fold selection, every modal LV and every refit model has at least this many components. Must satisfy 1 <= min_components < max_components; otherwise a ValueError names both values before any fold is fitted. Default: 1 (the unfloored rule; the trajectory latent space applies its own floor, see :func:motco.simulations.evaluation.fit_pls_latent_space).

1

Returns:

Type Description dict

With two keys:

  • "table": pd.DataFrame with one row per repeat and four columns — "rep" (int), "LV" (int, modal across K outer folds with parsimony tie-break), "AUROC" (float, mean across K outer folds), "AUROC_std" (float, sample std across K outer folds; NaN if K < 2).
  • "models": list of length n_repeats. Each entry is a PLSRegression refit on the full input (X, one-hot(y)) with the corresponding row's modal n_LV.

With nuisance given, a third key "nuisance_min_training_df" holds the smallest residual degrees of freedom of any training-set residualization fit.

        ``1 <= min_components < max_components``; otherwise a ``ValueError``
        names both values before any fold is fitted. Default: 1 (the
        unfloored rule; the trajectory latent space applies its own floor,
        see :func:`motco.simulations.evaluation.fit_pls_latent_space`).

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        With two keys:

        - ``"table"``: pd.DataFrame with one row per repeat and four columns —
          ``"rep"`` (int), ``"LV"`` (int, modal across K outer folds with
          parsimony tie-break), ``"AUROC"`` (float, mean across K outer folds),
          ``"AUROC_std"`` (float, sample std across K outer folds; NaN if K < 2).
        - ``"models"``: list of length ``n_repeats``. Each entry is a
          PLSRegression refit on the full input (X, one-hot(y)) with the
          corresponding row's modal n_LV.

        With ``nuisance`` given, a third key ``"nuisance_min_training_df"``
        holds the smallest residual degrees of freedom of any training-set
        residualization fit.
    """
    _X_arr = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    _y_arr = np.asarray(y)
    _n_x = _X_arr.shape[0]
    _n_y = _y_arr.shape[0]
    if _n_x != _n_y:
        raise ValueError(
            f"X has {_n_x} rows but y has {_n_y} rows — number of rows must match."
        )
    _n_classes = len(np.unique(_y_arr))
    if _n_classes < 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"y has {_n_classes} unique class(es); at least 2 are required."
        )
    if max_components > _X_arr.shape[1]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"max_components={max_components} exceeds the number of features in X "
            f"({_X_arr.shape[1]}); reduce max_components."
        )
    try:
        floor_ok = int(min_components) == min_components and 1 <= min_components < max_components
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        floor_ok = False
    if not floor_ok:
        raise ValueError(
            f"min_components={min_components!r} must be an integer with "
            f"1 <= min_components < max_components={max_components}; the candidates are "
            "min_components..max_components-1."
        )
    min_components = int(min_components)
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(_X_arr)):
        raise ValueError("X contains NaN or Inf values.")
    if nuisance is not None and nuisance.n_samples != _n_x:
        raise ValueError(f"X has {_n_x} rows but the nuisance design has {nuisance.n_samples}.")
    folds_on: Union[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series] = y
    if strata is not None:
        folds_on = pd.Series(np.asarray(strata))
        if folds_on.shape[0] != _n_x:
            raise ValueError(f"X has {_n_x} rows but strata has {folds_on.shape[0]}.")
    encoder = OneHotEncoder(sparse_output=False)
    yd_arr = encoder.fit_transform(np.array(y).reshape(-1, 1))
    yd = pd.DataFrame(yd_arr)
    cv2 = RepeatedStratifiedKFold(
        n_splits=cv2_splits, n_repeats=n_repeats, random_state=random_state
    )
    cv1 = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=cv1_splits)

    n_lv_candidates = list(range(min_components, max_components))
    n_candidates = len(n_lv_candidates)

    rep_means: list[float] = []
    rep_stds: list[float] = []
    rep_lvs: list[int] = []

    outer_aurocs: list[float] = []
    outer_n_lv: list[int] = []
    fold_in_repeat = 0
    training_dfs: list[int] = []
    auroc = partial(_plsda_auroc, scale=scale)

    cv2_iter = tqdm(
        cv2.split(X, folds_on),
        total=cv2_splits * n_repeats,
        desc="PLS-DA CV2",
        unit="fold",
        disable=not progress,
    )
    for rest, test in cv2_iter:
        X_rest = X.iloc[rest, :]
        X_test = X.iloc[test, :]
        folds_on_rest = folds_on.iloc[rest]
        yd_rest = yd.iloc[rest, :]
        yd_test = yd.iloc[test, :]
        outer_where = f"repeat {len(rep_lvs) + 1}, outer fold {fold_in_repeat + 1}"
        X_rest_fit, X_test_fit = X_rest, X_test
        if nuisance is not None:
            X_rest_fit, X_test_fit, rest_df = _fit_and_residualize(
                X_rest, X_test, nuisance, rest, test, outer_where
            )
            training_dfs.append(rest_df)

        # Inner CV: average AUROC across V folds for each candidate n_LV.
        inner_aurocs = np.zeros((cv1_splits, n_candidates))
        for v_idx, (train, validation) in enumerate(cv1.split(X_rest, folds_on_rest)):
            X_train = X_rest.iloc[train, :]
            yd_train = yd_rest.iloc[train, :]
            X_val = X_rest.iloc[validation, :]
            yd_val = yd_rest.iloc[validation, :]
            if nuisance is not None:
                # Coefficients from the inner training rows of the raw predictors.
                X_train, X_val, train_df = _fit_and_residualize(
                    X_train,
                    X_val,
                    nuisance,
                    rest[train],
                    rest[validation],
                    f"{outer_where}, inner fold {v_idx + 1}",
                )
                training_dfs.append(train_df)
            args = zip(
                n_lv_candidates,
                repeat(X_train),
                repeat(yd_train),
                repeat(X_val),
                repeat(yd_val),
            )
            fold_aurocs: list[float]
            if n_jobs == 1:
                fold_aurocs = [auroc(*a) for a in args]  # type: ignore[misc]
            else:
                n_workers = (
                    (multiprocessing.cpu_count() or 1) if n_jobs == -1 else max(1, n_jobs)
                )
                with multiprocessing.Pool(processes=n_workers) as pool:
                    fold_aurocs = pool.starmap(auroc, args)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            inner_aurocs[v_idx, :] = fold_aurocs

        mean_per_n_lv = inner_aurocs.mean(axis=0)
        # np.argmax returns the first occurrence on ties → parsimony. Select
        # by value so the floor is a property of the candidate set.
        n_lv_star = n_lv_candidates[int(np.argmax(mean_per_n_lv))]

        outer_score = float(
            auroc(n_lv_star, X_rest_fit, yd_rest, X_test_fit, yd_test)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        )
        outer_aurocs.append(outer_score)
        outer_n_lv.append(n_lv_star)

        fold_in_repeat += 1
        if fold_in_repeat == cv2_splits:
            mean_auroc = float(np.mean(outer_aurocs))
            std_auroc = (
                float(np.std(outer_aurocs, ddof=1))
                if len(outer_aurocs) > 1
                else float("nan")
            )
            mode_lv = _modal_int_with_parsimony(outer_n_lv)
            rep_means.append(mean_auroc)
            rep_stds.append(std_auroc)
            rep_lvs.append(mode_lv)
            outer_aurocs = []
            outer_n_lv = []
            fold_in_repeat = 0

    model_table = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "rep": list(range(1, n_repeats + 1)),
            "LV": rep_lvs,
            "AUROC": rep_means,
            "AUROC_std": rep_stds,
        }
    )
    model_table["rep"] = model_table["rep"].astype(int)
    model_table["LV"] = model_table["LV"].astype(int)
    model_table["AUROC"] = model_table["AUROC"].astype(float)
    model_table["AUROC_std"] = model_table["AUROC_std"].astype(float)

    X_full = _X_arr
    if nuisance is not None:
        try:
            full_coefficients, _ = fit_nuisance_coefficients(_X_arr, nuisance)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"Nuisance residualization failed on the full input: {exc}") from exc
        X_full = residualize(_X_arr, nuisance.covariates, full_coefficients)

    best_models: list[PLSRegression] = []
    for lv in rep_lvs:
        model = PLSRegression(
            n_components=lv, scale=scale, max_iter=1000
        ).fit(X_full, yd_arr)
        best_models.append(model)

    if nuisance is not None:
        return {"models": best_models, "table": model_table, "nuisance_min_training_df": min(training_dfs)}
    return {"models": best_models, "table": model_table}

def calculate_vips(
    model,
    components: Union[None, list[int]] = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Estimates Variable Importance in Projection (VIP)
    in Partial Least Squares (PLS)

    Parameters
    ----------
    model: PLSRegression
        model generated from the PLSRegression function
    components: Union[None, list[int]]
        if not None, a list of integers indicating the components to compute
        the VIPs from. If None, all components are taken into account.
        Default None.

    Returns
    -------
    vips: np.array
        variable importance in projection for each variable
    """
    if components is not None:
        t = model.x_scores_[:, components]
        w = model.x_weights_[:, components]
        q = model.y_loadings_[:, components]
        p, h = w.shape
    else:
        w = model.x_weights_
        t = model.x_scores_
        q = model.y_loadings_
        p, h = w.shape

    vips = np.zeros((p,))
    s = np.diag(np.matmul(np.matmul(np.matmul(t.T, t), q.T), q)).reshape(h, -1)
    total_s = np.sum(s)
    for i in range(p):
        weight = np.array([(w[i, j] / np.linalg.norm(w[:, j])) ** 2 for j in range(h)])
        vips[i] = np.sqrt(p * np.matmul(s.T, weight)[0] / total_s)
    return vips

docs.title: motco.stats.pls.NuisanceDesign dataclass
docs.text:
Row-aligned nuisance design for covariate residualization.

conditioning (n × k) holds the design the covariate coefficients are estimated conditional on (for example drop-first stage indicators), without an intercept; covariates (n × q) holds the covariate columns whose fitted part is removed. The residualization regresses each predictor on [1, conditioning, covariates] and subtracts only the covariate part, so signal collinear with the covariates but explained by the conditioning design is kept (Frisch–Waugh–Lovell). kind optionally names the conditioning design for callers that record it.

Source code in src/motco/stats/pls.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NuisanceDesign:
    """Row-aligned nuisance design for covariate residualization.

    ``conditioning`` (``n × k``) holds the design the covariate coefficients
    are estimated conditional on (for example drop-first stage indicators),
    without an intercept; ``covariates`` (``n × q``) holds the covariate
    columns whose fitted part is removed. The residualization regresses each
    predictor on ``[1, conditioning, covariates]`` and subtracts only the
    covariate part, so signal collinear with the covariates but explained by
    the conditioning design is kept (Frisch–Waugh–Lovell). ``kind`` optionally
    names the conditioning design for callers that record it.
    """

    conditioning: np.ndarray
    covariates: np.ndarray
    conditioning_names: tuple[str, ...]
    covariate_names: tuple[str, ...]
    kind: str | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        conditioning = np.asarray(self.conditioning, dtype=float)
        covariates = np.asarray(self.covariates, dtype=float)
        if conditioning.ndim != 2 or covariates.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError("NuisanceDesign conditioning and covariates must be 2-D matrices.")
        if conditioning.shape[0] != covariates.shape[0]:
            raise ValueError(
                f"NuisanceDesign conditioning has {conditioning.shape[0]} rows but covariates have "
                f"{covariates.shape[0]}."
            )
        if covariates.shape[1] == 0:
            raise ValueError("NuisanceDesign needs at least one covariate column.")
        if conditioning.shape[1] != len(self.conditioning_names) or covariates.shape[1] != len(
            self.covariate_names
        ):
            raise ValueError("NuisanceDesign column names do not match its matrices.")
        object.__setattr__(self, "conditioning", conditioning)
        object.__setattr__(self, "covariates", covariates)
        object.__setattr__(self, "conditioning_names", tuple(self.conditioning_names))
        object.__setattr__(self, "covariate_names", tuple(self.covariate_names))

    @property
    def n_samples(self) -> int:
        return int(self.covariates.shape[0])

    @property
    def column_names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Design column names beyond the intercept: conditioning, then covariates."""

        return self.conditioning_names + self.covariate_names

    def matrix(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """The full residualization design ``[1, conditioning, covariates]``."""

        return np.column_stack([np.ones(self.n_samples), self.conditioning, self.covariates])

    def cells(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """One label per row naming its conditioning cell (its distinct conditioning row).

        Under stage indicators these are the stages; under group × stage
        indicators, the group × stage cells. Used to stratify cross-validation
        folds so that every training set contains every conditioning cell.
        """

        return np.array(["|".join(f"{value:g}" for value in row) for row in self.conditioning], dtype=object)

    def rows(self, index: Union[np.ndarray, Sequence[int]]) -> "NuisanceDesign":
        """The design restricted to ``index`` (positional rows)."""

        index = np.asarray(index)
        return NuisanceDesign(
            self.conditioning[index], self.covariates[index], self.conditioning_names, self.covariate_names, self.kind
        )

docs.title: motco.stats.pls.fit_nuisance_coefficients(X, design)
docs.text:
Estimate the covariate coefficients of X conditional on the design.

Regresses every column of X on [1, conditioning, covariates] by least squares and returns the covariate block of the coefficients (q × p) and the residual degrees of freedom n − 1 − k − q.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If X and the design differ in rows, or the design does not have full column rank; the message names the design columns.

Source code in src/motco/stats/pls.py 
def fit_nuisance_coefficients(
    X: Union[np.ndarray, pd.DataFrame],
    design: NuisanceDesign,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:
    """Estimate the covariate coefficients of ``X`` conditional on the design.

    Regresses every column of ``X`` on ``[1, conditioning, covariates]`` by
    least squares and returns the covariate block of the coefficients
    (``q × p``) and the residual degrees of freedom ``n − 1 − k − q``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``X`` and the design differ in rows, or the design does not have
        full column rank; the message names the design columns.
    """

    X_arr = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    if X_arr.shape[0] != design.n_samples:
        raise ValueError(f"X has {X_arr.shape[0]} rows but the nuisance design has {design.n_samples}.")
    M = design.matrix()
    rank = int(np.linalg.matrix_rank(M))
    if rank < M.shape[1]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The residualization design [intercept, {', '.join(design.column_names)}] is not of full rank "
            f"(rank {rank} of {M.shape[1]} columns on {M.shape[0]} samples); a covariate is collinear with "
            "the conditioning design or with another covariate, or a factor level is absent."
        )
    coefficients = np.linalg.lstsq(M, X_arr, rcond=None)[0]
    k = design.conditioning.shape[1]
    return coefficients[1 + k :, :], int(M.shape[0] - M.shape[1])

def residualize(
    X: Union[np.ndarray, pd.DataFrame],
    covariates: np.ndarray,
    coefficients: np.ndarray,
) -> Union[np.ndarray, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Subtract the fitted covariate part: ``X − covariates @ coefficients``.

    Only the covariate columns are read, so held-out rows can be residualized
    with training coefficients without their labels. A DataFrame keeps its
    index and columns.
    """

    shift = np.asarray(covariates, dtype=float) @ np.asarray(coefficients, dtype=float)
    if isinstance(X, pd.DataFrame):
        return X - pd.DataFrame(shift, index=X.index, columns=X.columns)
    return np.asarray(X, dtype=float) - shift

docs.text:
Per-feature partial R² of the covariates given the intercept and conditioning.

1 − RSS([1, D, C]) / RSS([1, D]) for every column of X: the share of the variance left after the conditioning design that the covariates explain, i.e. what the residualization removes. A column with no variance left after the conditioning design gets 0.

Source code in src/motco/stats/pls.py 
def nuisance_partial_r2(X: Union[np.ndarray, pd.DataFrame], design: NuisanceDesign) -> np.ndarray:
    """Per-feature partial R² of the covariates given the intercept and conditioning.

    ``1 − RSS([1, D, C]) / RSS([1, D])`` for every column of ``X``: the share
    of the variance left after the conditioning design that the covariates
    explain, i.e. what the residualization removes. A column with no variance
    left after the conditioning design gets 0.
    """

    X_arr = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    full = design.matrix()
    reduced = full[:, : 1 + design.conditioning.shape[1]]
    rss_full = _residual_sum_of_squares(full, X_arr)
    rss_reduced = _residual_sum_of_squares(reduced, X_arr)
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        r2 = np.where(rss_reduced > 0.0, 1.0 - rss_full / rss_reduced, 0.0)
    return np.clip(r2, 0.0, 1.0)

docs.title: Trajectory Analysis
docs.text: Group trajectory differences: magnitude, orientation, and shape.

docs.title: Assumptions about the measurement space
docs.text:
The trajectory statistics use Euclidean geometry in the supplied outcome matrix. Their interpretation therefore depends on how that matrix was built.

Representation What the statistics directly describe Interpretation Standardized concatenation The complete standardized feature space A transparent baseline, but feature weighting depends on standardization and block dimensionality PCA or PLS scores A linear projection of the feature space Path length and direction can be related to the original features through the fitted loadings; omitted components still make the projection lossy SNF spectral coordinates A nonlinear embedding of a fused affinity graph Euclidean length, angle, and Procrustes shape describe the embedding and are not guaranteed to preserve feature-space geometry

delta and angle are most directly aligned with linear measurement spaces. When using SNF, validate the intended geometric interpretation by simulation and see Interpreting trajectory geometry in SNF space. Graph-native diffusion, connectivity, or transition-profile statistics would be a separate methodology and are not implemented by the current trajectory API.

docs.title: Interpreting shape
docs.text:
shape is a strict geometric-morphometric residual configuration statistic. For each group trajectory, MOTCO centers the stage configuration and scales it to unit centroid size. Pairwise shape distance is then the residual norm after aligning one trajectory to the other over the full orthogonal group — the alignment is unconstrained in determinant, so reflections are aligned away rather than retained.

Under this contract, translation, positive uniform scale, and any orthogonal transformation — proper rotation or reflection — do not produce nonzero shape distance beyond numerical tolerance. Genuine configuration changes, such as moving an interior stage so relative stage-to-stage distances change after size normalization, remain positive.

The reflection policy is uniform: it does not depend on whether the stage configuration spans the ambient space, so the statistic means the same thing at every measurement checkpoint. (A trajectory of k stages has rank at most k − 1, so in feature space a proper-rotation constraint would be satisfiable for free in the null space and therefore vacuous — the previous "reflections retained" contract bound only in a full-rank latent space.) A genuine mirror difference is an orientation difference and is reported by angle.

docs.title: Interpreting orientation and identifying feature drivers
docs.text:
In a shared linear PLS space, a trajectory orientation difference means that the groups progress through different relative combinations of the molecular patterns retained by PLS. Different stage-associated feature sets are one possible cause, but not the only one: the same features can change in different proportions or signs, or one group can recruit an additional correlated feature module.

For two stages, let each group's standardized feature-space transition be

d_g = mean(X | group=g, stage=1) - mean(X | group=g, stage=0)

or use covariate-adjusted LS means in place of raw means. To isolate direction from magnitude, normalize each transition and calculate

u_g = d_g / ||d_g||
q   = u_B - u_A

Large positive or negative values of q[j] identify features that contribute relatively more to one group's progression direction. With more than two stages, calculate this contrast for each adjacent transition and for the signed principal feature-space orientation used to summarize the complete path.

A production attribution analysis should:

  1. Keep the pooled preprocessing and PLS model fixed; do not fit independently aligned latent spaces for the two groups.
  2. Reconstruct each group's stage-to-stage PLS score displacement through the fitted X loadings, then compare the reconstructed normalized feature steps.
  3. Compare that loading-derived contrast with the directly observed or LS-mean-adjusted feature contrast q. Their agreement describes the part of the group difference captured by the retained PLS space; their residual describes feature variation that PLS omitted.
  4. Bootstrap samples to assess feature-rank and sign stability, especially for correlated features, and summarize stable signals at module/pathway level.
  5. Report standardized effects alongside original-unit effects. PLS geometry is defined after preprocessing, so raw-unit contributions need not have the same ranking.

Pooled VIP scores alone are insufficient for this question: they identify features important to the pooled stage model, not features whose normalized stage association differs between groups. Orientation drivers require the group-specific transition contrast above.

For a production attribution result from a detected orientation difference, use the shared fitted PLS model and the aligned pooled-standardized matrix with Orientation Driver Attribution. The attribution API supports adjacent transitions for multi-stage data, optional covariate- adjusted mean tables, frozen-model bootstrap stability, and caller-supplied module/pathway labels. It reports standardized and optional original-unit effects separately and does not produce p-values, causal claims, or a unique inverse of the measured features.

def get_model_matrix(
    X: pd.DataFrame,
    group_col: str,
    level_col: str,
    full: bool = True,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Build a design (model) matrix for group × level factors.

    Coding scheme
    -------------
    - Intercept (column of ones).
    - Group main effects: one-hot with drop-first for groups (G-1 columns).
    - Level main effects: one-hot with drop-first for levels (L-1 columns).
    - If `full=True`, include all interaction terms between group and level
      dummies: (G-1) × (L-1) columns.

    The category order is deterministic: numeric when every distinct label of
    a factor parses as an integer (so 10+ levels order correctly), otherwise
    sorted by string representation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X: pd.DataFrame
        DataFrame containing `group_col` and `level_col`.
    group_col: str
        Name of the group column.
    level_col: str
        Name of the level/state column.
    full: bool
        Whether to include interaction terms.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Model matrix with intercept.
    """
    for col, param in [(group_col, "group_col"), (level_col, "level_col")]:
        if col not in X.columns:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{param}='{col}' not found in X. Available columns: {list(X.columns)}."
            )
        n_unique = X[col].nunique()
        if n_unique < 2:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{param}='{col}' has {n_unique} unique value(s); at least 2 are required."
            )
    # Determine deterministic category order
    g_levels = _sort_levels(pd.unique(X[group_col].astype(str)).tolist())
    l_levels = _sort_levels(pd.unique(X[level_col].astype(str)).tolist())
    # Wrap in Series to preserve X.index; pd.get_dummies on a bare Categorical
    # returns integer-indexed DataFrames, which causes pd.concat to outer-join with
    # the string-indexed Intercept part and double the row count.
    g = pd.Series(
        pd.Categorical(X[group_col].astype(str), categories=g_levels, ordered=True),
        index=X.index,
    )
    lc = pd.Series(
        pd.Categorical(X[level_col].astype(str), categories=l_levels, ordered=True),
        index=X.index,
    )

    G = pd.get_dummies(g, drop_first=True, dtype=int)
    L = pd.get_dummies(lc, drop_first=True, dtype=int)

    parts = []
    # Intercept
    parts.append(pd.DataFrame({"Intercept": np.ones(len(X))}, index=X.index))
    # Main effects
    if G.shape[1] > 0:
        parts.append(G)
    if L.shape[1] > 0:
        parts.append(L)
    # Interactions
    if full and G.shape[1] > 0 and L.shape[1] > 0:
        inter_cols = {}
        for g_col in G.columns:
            for l_col in L.columns:
                inter_cols[f"{g_col}:{l_col}"] = np.asarray(G[g_col]) * np.asarray(L[l_col])
        parts.append(pd.DataFrame(inter_cols, index=X.index))

    model_mat = pd.concat(parts, axis=1).to_numpy()
    return model_mat

LS-mean design matrix with shape (G×L, 1 + (G-1) + (L-1) + I), where I = (G-1)×(L-1) if full=True else 0. Row order is by group major, then level minor.

Source code in src/motco/stats/design.py 
def build_ls_means(
    group_levels: Sequence[str],
    level_levels: Sequence[str],
    full: bool = True,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Generate LS-mean rows for every group × level cell consistent with
    `get_model_matrix` coding.

    Parameters
    ----------
    group_levels: Sequence[str]
        Sorted group labels; first is baseline.
    level_levels: Sequence[str]
        Sorted level labels; first is baseline.
    full: bool
        Whether to include interaction terms.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        LS-mean design matrix with shape (G×L, 1 + (G-1) + (L-1) + I), where
        I = (G-1)×(L-1) if `full=True` else 0. Row order is by group major,
        then level minor.
    """
    g_levels = list(group_levels)
    l_levels = list(level_levels)
    Gm1 = max(len(g_levels) - 1, 0)
    Lm1 = max(len(l_levels) - 1, 0)
    n_rows = max(len(g_levels), 1) * max(len(l_levels), 1)
    n_cols = 1 + Gm1 + Lm1 + (Gm1 * Lm1 if full else 0)
    M = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)

    def row_for(i_g: int, i_l: int) -> int:
        return i_g * len(l_levels) + i_l

    # Column indices
    col = 0
    INTERCEPT = col
    col += 1
    G_START = col
    col += Gm1
    L_START = col
    col += Lm1
    I_START = col if full else None

    for gi, g_val in enumerate(g_levels):
        for li, l_val in enumerate(l_levels):
            r = row_for(gi, li)
            # Intercept
            M[r, INTERCEPT] = 1.0
            # Group dummies (drop first)
            if gi > 0 and Gm1 > 0:
                M[r, G_START + (gi - 1)] = 1.0
            # Level dummies (drop first)
            if li > 0 and Lm1 > 0:
                M[r, L_START + (li - 1)] = 1.0
            # Interactions
            if full and gi > 0 and li > 0 and (Gm1 > 0 and Lm1 > 0):
                assert I_START is not None
                idx = (gi - 1) * Lm1 + (li - 1)
                M[r, I_START + idx] = 1.0
    return M

def center_matrix(
    dat: pd.DataFrame,
    group_col: str,
    level_col: str,
    feature_cols: Sequence[str] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Center feature columns by per-group means.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dat: pd.DataFrame
        Original, non-centered dataframe.
    group_col: str
        Column in `dat` indicating the group (between-subject factor).
    level_col: str
        Column in `dat` indicating the level/state (within-group factor).
    feature_cols: Sequence[str] | None
        Feature columns to center. If None, all numeric columns except
        `group_col` and `level_col` are used.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        A copy of `dat` with selected feature columns centered within groups.
    """
    if feature_cols is not None:
        missing = [c for c in feature_cols if c not in dat.columns]
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"feature_cols contains column(s) not found in dat: {missing}."
            )
    datc = dat.copy()
    if feature_cols is None:
        feature_cols = [
            c
            for c in datc.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()
            if c not in {group_col, level_col}
        ]
    if not feature_cols:
        return datc
    # Center within groups using group-wise means
    datc.loc[:, feature_cols] = (
        datc.loc[:, feature_cols]
        - datc.groupby(group_col)[feature_cols].transform("mean")
    )
    return datc

def estimate_betas(
    X: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray], Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
) -> Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Estimate the beta coefficients between an outcome matrix
    and a model matrix

    Parameters
    ----------
    X: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Model matrix with intercept.
    Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Outcome matrix.

    Returns
    -------
    betas: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Beta coefficients
    """
    # Convert inputs to arrays for linear algebra while preserving Y's metadata
    X_arr = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    if isinstance(Y, pd.DataFrame):
        Y_arr = Y.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        y_cols = Y.columns
    else:
        Y_arr = np.asarray(Y, dtype=float)
        y_cols = None

    # Solve normal equations using factorization with robust fallbacks
    XtX = X_arr.T @ X_arr
    XtY = X_arr.T @ Y_arr
    try:
        # Cholesky is fastest and most stable for SPD XtX
        L = np.linalg.cholesky(XtX)
        tmp = np.linalg.solve(L, XtY)
        betas_arr = np.linalg.solve(L.T, tmp)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        logger.warning("Cholesky decomposition failed; falling back to direct solve. Check for near-singular XtX.")
        try:
            # Fall back to a direct solve of the normal equations
            betas_arr = np.linalg.solve(XtX, XtY)
        except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
            logger.warning("Direct solve failed; falling back to lstsq. Model matrix may be rank-deficient.")
            # Final fallback: least-squares without forming normal equations
            # This handles rank deficiency and ill-conditioning better.
            betas_arr, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(X_arr, Y_arr, rcond=None)

    if y_cols is not None:
        # Return a DataFrame so downstream matmul with numpy yields a DataFrame
        # and index/column handling stays consistent with previous behavior.
        return pd.DataFrame(betas_arr, columns=y_cols)
    return betas_arr

def get_observed_vectors(
    X: pd.DataFrame,
    Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray],
    group_col: str,
    level_col: str,
    full: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Get LS-mean vectors for each group × level cell.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X: pd.DataFrame
        DataFrame containing factors `group_col` and `level_col` for each row
        corresponding to `Y`.
    Y: Union[pd.DataFrame, np.ndarray]
        Outcome matrix (n_samples × n_features).
    group_col: str
        Group column name in `X`.
    level_col: str
        Level/state column name in `X`.
    full: bool
        Whether to include interactions in the model.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        LS means arranged with a MultiIndex (group, level). Columns follow `Y`.
    """
    model_full = get_model_matrix(X[[group_col, level_col]], group_col, level_col, full)
    betas = estimate_betas(model_full, Y)

    g_levels = _sort_levels(pd.unique(X[group_col].astype(str)).tolist())
    l_levels = _sort_levels(pd.unique(X[level_col].astype(str)).tolist())
    ls_matrix = build_ls_means(g_levels, l_levels, full)
    means = np.matmul(ls_matrix, np.asarray(betas, dtype=float))

    # Build a clear index and columns
    idx = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([g_levels, l_levels], names=[group_col, level_col])
    if isinstance(Y, pd.DataFrame):
        cols = Y.columns
    else:
        cols = [f"f{i}" for i in range(means.shape[1])]  # type: ignore[assignment]
    return pd.DataFrame(means, index=idx, columns=cols)
