docs.text:
Pooled over the 14 cells of each column, as a share of the available units:

column arm rank 2 rank 3 rank ≥ 4 rank 1 nuisance baseline 0.381 0.513 0.106 0 nuisance stage 0.048 0.842 0.110 0 nuisance group_stage 0.010 0.984 0.006 0 clean baseline 0.341 0.621 0.038 0 clean stage 0.045 0.853 0.102 0 clean group_stage 0.008 0.987 0.005 0

Per-cell distributions are in the rank_distribution column of the rates table. Residualization moves the CV almost entirely off rank 2. No unit in any arm or column selected rank 1. This construction therefore does not reproduce the SEA-AD cohorts' rank-1 selection and is not evidence about it. The separate rank-1 angle change needs a construction with a single dominant axis, or real-data evidence (roadmap, Next changes item 4).

docs.title: 5. Reading
docs.text:
• Residualization removes signal even when no covariate has an effect. On six clean-column orientation replicates at e = 1.0 (a diagnostic run on the workstation, not part of the records), the subtracted term C γ carries about 19 % of each pooled-standardized feature's variance under stage and about 12 % under group_stage.
  • Under stage, z differs by group within each stage by construction (a_g + a_gs·s), so γ takes in part of the group difference. About a quarter of the features' between-cell (group × stage) variance is removed from the features the basis is fitted on.
  • Under group_stage, 12 % is what nine covariates fit by chance on 74 within-cell degrees of freedom. About 40 % of it lands between cells, because z's cell means run from 0.56 to 6.94 against a within-cell SD of about 0.9, so the estimation error of γ is extrapolated into a spurious cell-mean pattern.
  • The basis is then fitted, at the pooled scale, on features that carry that spurious pattern. This is consistent with, though not proof of, group_stage's loss of orientation and shape power and its control excesses.
  • stage's profile is a trade. It finds the orientation surgery far more often in both columns, and the shape surgery more often in the clean column. It finds small magnitude effects and the shape surgery less often when the nuisance axis is present. delta rejects less often under shape and orientation effects. Because the orientation gain also appears with no nuisance effect at all, it is not simply the nuisance axis being removed. The basis changes whenever the covariates are confounded with group within stage, as they are here by construction.
  • The nuisance axis also inflates the covariate-blind basis's power. Its shape rate at e = 1.0 is 0.428 with the axis and 0.128 without, and its orientation angle rate is 0.784 against 0.642. Part of stage's protected-pair shape "loss" is therefore a loss against a nuisance-inflated reference, consistent with the baseline's anchor shape of 0.078 above its bound in the Type I check. The rule does not distinguish the two, and this report does not overrule it.
  • The translation control. angle under a pure location shift is at or above the bound for every arm here, including the covariate-blind basis (0.076 and 0.086). The net-displacement power comparison already placed translation near the bound (0.058–0.068) without covariates. With eight covariates this construction pushes all arms above it, stage by a further 0.016 in the nuisance column.

docs.title: 6. Scope, limits and consequence
docs.text:
• Mediators. Residualizing a variable that mediates the stage effect removes real signal. No simulation can tell a confounder from a mediator; this comparison injects a pure confounder. The case study must choose and justify its covariate set in its own proposal.
  • Extreme confounding. The covariates here are confounded with group × stage far beyond what technical variables usually are: z's cell means span about 7 within-cell SDs. The power costs above, and the group_stage failure, grow with that confounding. Real covariates that are less tied to the design will remove less signal, but this comparison does not measure how much less.
  • One design. n = 80, two blocks, 498 features, eight covariates, one injected direction per covariate.
  • Advisory. The verdicts are advisory; the Type I decision (adopt_stage) is the gate.

Consequence for the case study. --latent-adjustment stage remains size-valid (Type I report §5). It is not a power upgrade to adopt instead of the covariate-adjusted 0.8.0 analysis:

  • report it as a sensitivity analysis beside the 0.8.0 analysis on the same covariates, not as a replacement;
  • read an angle rejection that appears only under latent adjustment in light of the translation control above, which is at or above the bound for both bases;
  • treat a delta or shape non-rejection under latent adjustment as weaker than under the covariate-blind basis;
  • report the record's latent_adjustment block, in particular feature_r2, which shows how much variance the residualization removed;
  • do not use group_stage.

docs.title: Latent-adjustment Type I check — 2026-10-20
docs.text:
Paper-grade size check of covariate-aware latent construction (covariate_latent_adjustment, motco analyze --latent-adjustment) at the Phase 6 SEA-AD design (openspec/changes/covariate-aware-latent-construction/, design D8, spec latent-adjustment-validation). It is the gate the case study must pass before it reports latent-adjusted trajectory results. Every number below is read from results/latent-adjustment-type-i-2026-10-20/ (latent_adjustment_type_i_decision.json, latent_adjustment_type_i_rates.csv, latent_adjustment_type_i_pvalues.csv, latent_adjustment_type_i_replicates.csv, merged.jsonl). Rates are rejection rates at p ≤ 0.05 over the available replicates of 500, at 999 permutations.

Run: 500 replicates on ing (SLURM arrays 923443 and 923539, 50 shards, 5.1 recorded core-hours), from 979657c plus this change's working tree; file hashes are in PROVENANCE.txt. Decision: adopt_stage. The admissible conditionings are stage only.

In one paragraph. Null datasets at the SEA-AD MTG design carried two covariates confounded with group × stage, whose effect was injected strongly enough that the covariate-blind basis spends its first latent component on the numeric covariate: median |Spearman| 0.83 between that component and the covariate. Each replicate was analysed with eight covariates declared, in three arms that differ only in how the basis is built. With stage conditioning, the three statistics hold the predeclared bound: delta 0.031, angle 0.067 and shape 0.058 against 0.0706 (R = 448). With group_stage conditioning, angle exceeds it: 0.082 against 0.0703 (R = 462). Residualization moved the first component off the covariate (median |ρ| 0.34). The case study may use --latent-adjustment stage under the conditions in §5, and not group_stage.

docs.title: 1. Construction
docs.text:
• Data and covariates. The covariate-adjustment check's construction (report §1), imported from scripts/covariate_type_i_check.py rather than copied. The data are generate_semisynthetic_trajectory at the phase6_small_n settings: three stages, group_stage_sizes = [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]], methylation (M-values) and expression blocks, 498 features, group_effect_size = 0. A numeric z and a three-level factor depend on group, stage and their interaction (a_g = 0.5, a_s = 1, a_gs = 2, logit scale 0.5).
  • The seeds are the covariate check's (base seed 2026). Replicate r therefore draws the same generated blocks, z and factor as that check's replicate r.
  • Noise covariates. Six i.i.d. N(0, 1) numeric covariates x1–x6, declared but never injected, are drawn from their own seed. Every arm therefore declares 8 covariates (9 design columns). This puts the residualization at the case study's 8–10 covariates and its inner CV folds at the case study's degrees of freedom (design, Risks).
  • Injection. X_f += s_z·sd_f·w_f·z + s_c·sd_f·Σ_k u_{k,f}·1[cat = k] on a random 20 % of features per direction. The strengths are s_z = 40 (calibrated, below) and s_c = 2.
  • Arms. Each replicate runs analyze_trajectories three times with the same covariates, CV settings (harness defaults) and RRPP seed, and the net-displacement estimator:
  • baseline: covariates in the trajectory model only, with the covariate-blind basis (the 0.8.0 analysis);
  • stage: covariate_latent_adjustment="stage";
  • group_stage: covariate_latent_adjustment="group_stage".
  • Rule. For each residualized arm and statistic, the rate over the R available replicates must be at most α + k·√(α(1 − α)/R), with α = 0.05 and k = 2. An arm is admissible when all three statistics hold. The decision is adopt_stage when stage is admissible, adopt_group_stage when only group_stage is, and otherwise diagnose_latent_excess. The baseline arm is reported only.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
The gate needs the covariate-blind basis to be spent on the nuisance axis. The criterion is a median |Spearman| of at least 0.8 between the first component's scores and z, checked on the smoke profile before any paper-grade run. At the covariate check's s_z = 3, the median over the 20 smoke replicates was 0.64. It rises with s_z and then saturates: 0.74 at 6, 0.78 at 10, 0.80 at 20, 0.81 at 30 and 0.815 at 40. The covariate-blind fit re-standardizes every feature, so once the injected features are dominated by z a stronger injection adds nothing; only the injected fifth of the features can carry z. s_z = 40 was chosen for the most margin. The smoke profile (R = 20, 99 permutations) confirmed 0.815.

In the paper-grade run the baseline median |ρ| is 0.830 (5–95 % range 0.751–0.891; minimum 0.708), so the criterion is met. The covariate-blind basis selected rank 2 in 265 replicates, rank 3 in 233 and rank 4 in 2.

docs.title: 2. Rates against the bound
docs.text:
From latent_adjustment_type_i_rates.csv. Rate (Monte Carlo SE).

statistic stage (R = 448, bound 0.0706) group_stage (R = 462, bound 0.0703) baseline (R = 500, descriptive) delta 0.031 (0.0082) holds 0.048 (0.0099) holds 0.048 (0.0096) angle 0.067 (0.0118) holds 0.082 (0.0128) exceeds 0.062 (0.0108) shape 0.058 (0.0110) holds 0.069 (0.0118) holds 0.078 (0.0120)

At p < 0.05 instead of p ≤ 0.05, every rate is the same except group_stage angle, which is 0.078 and still exceeds. The decision is unchanged.

Stability. In five consecutive blocks of 100 replicates (rates over each block's available replicates):

  • stage: delta 0.04, 0.01, 0.03, 0.03, 0.03; angle 0.03, 0.06, 0.07, 0.13, 0.04; shape 0.05, 0.07, 0.06, 0.04, 0.07.
  • group_stage: delta 0.04, 0.02, 0.09, 0.04, 0.04; angle 0.05, 0.10, 0.05, 0.14, 0.06; shape 0.07, 0.07, 0.08, 0.07, 0.06.

In both arms the angle rate is driven by block 4, replicates 300–399. The covariate check's adjusted arm, on the same generated datasets, also had its angle excess in block 4 (0.11). The stage arm's 0.067 sits 0.004 below its bound; group_stage's 0.082 sits 0.012 above, and its block 2 is also high.

Unavailable replicates. An arm is unavailable for a replicate when a CV training design loses full rank.

  • That happened in 52 stage replicates and 38 group_stage replicates (22 in both), never in the baseline arm.
  • Every one is an inner-fold training set short exactly one column, an absent level of the three-level factor. They are spread across the five CV repeats (repeat 1 most often).
  • Excluding them does not flatter the residualized arms. On the replicates stage lost, the always-available baseline arm rejects delta 0.019, angle 0.019 and shape 0.096 (n = 52). On the replicates stage kept, it rejects delta 0.051, angle 0.067 and shape 0.076 (n = 448), close to its overall 0.048 / 0.062 / 0.078.
  • The group_stage comparison is similar: 0.026 / 0.026 / 0.132 on n = 38, against 0.050 / 0.065 / 0.074.

docs.title: 3. What residualization changes
docs.text:
• The basis. The first component's median |ρ| with z falls from 0.830 (baseline) to 0.336 (stage) and 0.355 (group_stage). The residualized bases no longer spend their first component on the nuisance axis; what correlation remains is the stage structure z shares by construction.
  • The rank. CV selects rank 3 in 417 of 448 stage replicates and 457 of 462 group_stage replicates, against 233 of 500 for the baseline. With the nuisance axis gone, the CV keeps more of the stage structure.
  • Degrees of freedom. The full-sample residual df is 68 under stage (80 − 1 − 2 − 9) and 65 under group_stage. The smallest CV training-set df is 28 and 25 in every replicate.
  • What is removed. The per-feature partial R² of the covariates given the conditioning design has a replicate-median of 0.13 (median feature), 0.27 (mean) and 0.99 (95th percentile). About 18 % of features have R² above 0.5, roughly the fifth of features that carry z.
  • The baseline arm. Here the 0.8.0 covariate adjustment alone, on the covariate-blind basis, lets shape reach 0.078. That is above the 0.0695 bound it would face at R = 500, and its rule does not judge it. The covariate check's adjusted arm held shape at 0.034 with s_z = 3 and two covariates. With a nuisance strong enough to take the first component, the model adjustment alone is no longer enough for shape, and latent adjustment is. This is descriptive, not a verdict.

docs.title: 4. Scope and limits
docs.text:
• Mediators. Residualizing a variable that mediates the stage effect removes real signal. No simulation can tell a confounder from a mediator, because the data look the same; this check injects a pure confounder. Choosing and justifying the covariate set is the case study's job, in its own proposal. A technical variable that is itself downstream of disease stage, such as a cell-quality metric that worsens with pathology, is a mediator candidate.
  • Additive, linear effects. The covariate effects are additive and linear, and correctly specified in the residualization and the model. Non-linear effects and covariate × design interactions are outside the check.
  • One design. n = 80, two blocks, 498 features, 8 covariates with 9 design columns, and one injected direction per covariate.
  • angle is near the bound. stage holds angle by 0.004, with one 100-replicate block at 0.13. Treat a marginal latent-adjusted angle rejection with the care the earlier reports ask of angle near the translation control.
  • Rare factor levels. About 10 % of replicates lose an arm to a factor level absent from a CV training set, and which fold fails depends on random_state. Merge rare levels before analysis; the record names the failing repeat and fold.
  • No power claim. This report covers size only. Power, with and without a nuisance axis, is the subject of the separate power comparison.

docs.title: 5. Consequence for the case study
docs.text:
The decision is adopt_stage. The SEA-AD case study may report latent-adjusted motco analyze results with --latent-adjustment stage (MOTCO ≥ 0.9.0) under these conditions:

  • its own proposal names and justifies the covariate set, including why no residualized variable mediates the stage effect;
  • group_stage conditioning is not used: it exceeded the bound on angle;
  • the record's latent_adjustment block (conditioning, design columns, residual df, smallest CV training df, the feature R² summary) and its covariates block are reported beside the results;
  • categorical covariates have no level rare enough to drop out of a CV training set;
  • the earlier binding statements stand: the CV-selected rank is reported beside angle, and non-rejections are uninformative;
  • the power comparison §6 applies: latent adjustment is a sensitivity analysis beside the covariate-adjusted analysis, not a replacement for it.

docs.title: The recorded eigengap reproduces the audit's association — and stratifies the orientation shortfall
docs.text: Run date: 2026-09-02 Code revision: working tree of the record-latent-config-spectrum change, parent 84061bdec824da9c33865d52e59a13b3750fb9fb (the merge of the geometry audit) Configuration: examples/trajectory_power_study/angle_pivotality_diagnostic.json — byte-identical to the 2026-09-01 diagnostic run (same SHA-256, 2dfa5cc3…) Records: results/latent-spectrum-2026-09-02/merged.jsonl (500 replicates, 0 failures, 199 permutations each, 500 of 500 carrying the configuration-spectrum block) Tables: results/latent-spectrum-2026-09-02/report/ — pivotality_spectrum.csv, eigengap_stratified_power.csv, config_spectrum.csv, plus the pre-existing pivotality and study tables Provenance: results/latent-spectrum-2026-09-02/PROVENANCE.txt Change: openspec/changes/record-latent-config-spectrum Answers: Phase 5 readiness items 1 (left-open gap), 3, and 4 (stratifying covariate); geometry audit plan item P1 Environment: Python 3.11.15, numpy 2.3.5, pandas 2.3.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0, scipy 1.16.3; no R at runtime

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The pivotality report established that an orientation replicate's outcome is decided by the width of its own angle permutation null, and stated that "nothing the harness records today identifies which replicates will be resolvable". The geometry audit (finding F1) named the missing quantity — the relative eigengap (λ₁−λ₂)/Σλ of the centered latent stage-mean configuration — by regenerating replicates from persisted seeds. This run persists that quantity per replicate and re-measures the association from the record alone.

Three results, all from the same 500 records:

  1. The audit's association reproduces. In the orientation cell, Spearman(pooled eigengap, own angle null q95) = −0.749 [−0.824, −0.648]; log–log Pearson −0.622. The audit measured −0.75 and −0.62.
  2. It is specific to angle. In the same cell the association with the delta and shape null widths is +0.093 [−0.105, +0.284] and −0.032 [−0.227, +0.166] — both intervals cover zero.
  3. It stratifies the shortfall. Orientation angle power rises monotonically across within-cell eigengap terciles: 0.44 → 0.76 → 0.85. The overall 0.68 is an average over a covariate the harness now records.

And the change is inert: every rejection rate and every pivotality slope reproduces the 2026-09-01 run exactly.

docs.title: 1. The association, measured from records
docs.text:
pivotality_spectrum.csv, null_target = q95, n = 100 per cell. Spearman with a Fisher-z 95% interval:

Cell delta angle shape none (zero effect) −0.092 −0.814 [−0.871, −0.735] −0.108 translation @1.00 (type_i_baseline) +0.019 −0.740 [−0.817, −0.636] +0.163 translation @1.00 (power_primary) +0.053 −0.836 [−0.887, −0.765] +0.009 magnitude @1.00 −0.086 −0.701 [−0.789, −0.586] −0.038 orientation @1.00 +0.093 −0.749 [−0.824, −0.648] −0.032

Every angle interval excludes zero by a wide margin; no delta or shape interval does. Log–log Pearson tells the same story for angle (−0.61 to −0.71 across cells; −0.622 in the orientation cell).

Read this as a property of the geometry, not of the effect. The association is present in the zero-effect baseline and in both translation controls at essentially the same strength. That is what the audit's mechanism predicts: PC1's estimator variance scales like noise over the eigengap, so a near-isotropic stage configuration yields a wide angle null whether or not a group difference was constructed. The recorded eigengap therefore predicts resolvability, and it does so without seeing the group labels.

docs.title: 2. It stratifies the orientation shortfall
docs.text:
eigengap_stratified_power.csv, orientation @1.00, α = 0.05, within-cell terciles of the recorded pooled eigengap:

Stratum eigengap range mean eigengap n angle rejections rate MC SE bottom 0.0057 – 0.0359 0.0243 34 15 0.44 0.085 middle 0.0364 – 0.0552 0.0451 33 25 0.76 0.075 top 0.0556 – 0.1173 0.0739 33 28 0.85 0.062

A 3× separation in eigengap maps to a 0.41 separation in power (SE of the difference 0.105). The cell's headline 0.68 is an average over this spread: replicates whose latent stage configuration has a dominant axis clear the 0.80 floor; those whose configuration is near-isotropic do not, and no amount of signal in a direction the configuration cannot resolve will move them.

The recorded distributions (config_spectrum.csv) show how tight the regime is. Pooled eigengaps per cell:

Cell mean median min max orientation @1.00 0.0475 0.0444 0.0057 0.1173 magnitude @1.00 0.0422 0.0406 0.0028 0.1612 translation @1.00 (power_primary) 0.0431 0.0404 0.0080 0.1126 translation @1.00 (type_i_baseline) 0.0532 0.0537 0.0030 0.1670 none 0.0450 0.0409 0.0022 0.1248

Every cell sits near the isotropic end (a straight trajectory would read 1.0), and the per-group entries agree with the pooled ones — consistent with the audit's account that the independent-indicator baseline, not the trajectory surgery, sets the eigengap. That is the lever readiness item 4 hands to baseline continuity (plan item P4), and it is now measured per replicate rather than inferred.

docs.title: 3. The change is inert
docs.text:
The config is byte-identical to the 2026-09-01 diagnostic, so the operating point is directly comparable. Every published number reproduces:

Quantity 2026-09-01 this run orientation angle / delta / shape power 0.68 / 0.65 / 0.99 0.68 / 0.65 / 0.99 magnitude delta / angle / shape 1.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 1.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 Type I none (delta/angle/shape, combined) — 0.04 / 0.05 / 0.01, 0.09 angle null-tracking slope: none / translation (t1b, pp) / magnitude / orientation 0.931 / 0.925, 0.960 / 0.874 / 0.811 0.931 / 0.925, 0.960 / 0.874 / 0.811 orientation delta / shape slope 0.018 / 0.058 0.018 / 0.058

Reproduction to three decimals on every slope, and to the replicate on every rate. The spectrum consumes no randomness: it is computed from the LS-mean vectors estimate_difference already fits, after the permutation index is drawn. Unit tests pin the permutation draws and null distributions as byte-identical with the recording flag on and off, serially and in parallel (tests/test_trajectory_spectrum.py).

Cost. One SVD of a k×d matrix per configuration. On this design point (4 stages, rank-3 PLS latent space) recording the per-permutation eigengap adds ~12 ms to a 199-permutation RRPP — under 0.1% of a ~14 s replicate, which is dominated by the PLS double cross-validation.

docs.title: 4. What this does and does not change
docs.text:
• Nothing statistical. No statistic, p-value, permutation draw, generator behaviour, integration method, or latent-space sizing changed. The eigengap is a recorded covariate and a reporting qualifier — never a filter, weight, or test modification.
  • The audit's caution stands. The spectrum is only observed. Any group-aware sizing or supervision would void the fixed-latent-space RRPP conditioning; nothing here reads the group labels.
  • Resume policy changed deliberately. parameter_signature now includes config_spectrum_version, so a shard written before this change refuses resume rather than producing a merged set in which only some records carry the covariate. Already-merged pre-change record sets still load (empty block) and their committed reports are unaffected — verified by reporting a pre-change record set under the new code and finding specificity_matrix.csv, power_curves.csv, type_i_table.csv, acceptance_report.csv, and acceptance_report.json byte-identical to the pre-change code's output.

docs.title: Reproduction
docs.text:
# 5 cells x 100 replicates = 500 work units; ~50 minutes on 16 local shards.
for i in $(seq 0 15); do
  uv run python scripts/run_study_shard.py \
    --config examples/trajectory_power_study/angle_pivotality_diagnostic.json \
    --out-dir results/latent-spectrum-2026-09-02 \
    --shard-index "$i" --n-shards 16 --error-policy record &
done
wait
uv run python scripts/motco_study.py merge --out-dir results/latent-spectrum-2026-09-02
uv run python scripts/motco_study.py report \
  --config examples/trajectory_power_study/angle_pivotality_diagnostic.json \
  --out-dir results/latent-spectrum-2026-09-02
uv run python scripts/angle_null_pivotality.py \
  --merged  results/latent-spectrum-2026-09-02/merged.jsonl \
  --out-dir results/latent-spectrum-2026-09-02/report

Do not pass --n-jobs: it is part of the cell parameter signature. The shard and merged JSONL are gitignored as regenerable; report/ and PROVENANCE.txt are committed.

docs.title: Phase 5 latent-rank ladder — findings (run 2026-09-08)
docs.text:
Question (readiness item 3). At the Phase 5 design point, does retaining more PLS components than the stage-supervised double CV selects buy orientation angle power, and what does it cost magnitude, shape, and Type I error? Which group-blind rank rule does Phase 5 commit to?

Verdict: keep_cv. No fixed rank qualifies under the predeclared rule (report/rank_decision.json). Forced 3 is indistinguishable from the CV column; every rank above 3 loses shape power by 0.05–0.43 and gains no angle power. The committed Phase 5 rank rule is stage-supervised double cross-validation (plsda_doubleCV, modal LV across repeats, parsimony tie-break), as in production. At the design point it selects rank 3 = n_stages − 1 (range 2–3 across 1,500 CV units).

Every number below is read from results/phase5-latent-rank-2026-09-08/report/ (CSV/JSON) or from PROVENANCE.txt in the same directory.

docs.title: 1. Configuration and provenance
docs.text:
Item Value Source Config examples/trajectory_power_study/phase5_latent_rank_ladder.json PROVENANCE.txt Config sha256 b91339f9a8db9ee33d177e9fd9084d5c34e28d5ad2482fc47e4e25232fe31b5f PROVENANCE.txt Code a3ea2b4 (main) + the working tree of OpenSpec change resolve-latent-rank-at-design-point, tracked-file diff sha256 16afc68c…6ed1, synced to the cluster by rsync PROVENANCE.txt Design point ρ = 0, n_samples = 1200, four stages, p_dmp = 0.1, surgery_censoring = error (default) config Integration pooled PLS on M-value methylation; CV knobs cv1_splits 3, cv2_splits 4, n_repeats 5, max_components 20, random_state 1203 config Rank axis evaluation.integration_params.forced_components ∈ {null, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12}; null = CV config Modes × effects magnitude, orientation, shape, translation × {0.25, 0.50, 1.00} + one zero-effect anchor per column config Replicates × permutations 100 × 199; matched seeds (family phase5-latent-rank), shared anchor config Units 80 cells × 100 = 8,000; 8,000 present once, 0 signature mismatches, 0 failures, 0 censored surgeries, 0 duplicated constructions PROVENANCE.txt, realized_surgery.csv Compute SLURM 512x1024, 100 single-CPU shards, BLAS pinned, no --n-jobs; wall 20 min; CV units median 57.4 s (24.1 core-h), forced units median 0.2 s (0.3 core-h) PROVENANCE.txt Versions python 3.11.16, motco 0.6.0, numpy 2.3.5, scikit-learn 1.8.0, scipy 1.16.3 PROVENANCE.txt

Same data, different measurement. The rank axis is an evaluation-namespace axis, so all six columns share the primary matched-seed family and identical generator parameters: at every replicate index they evaluate the same generated dataset at a different retained rank (rank_decision.json, pairing). Differences between columns are measurement differences. The rule's pooled independent SE is therefore conservative.

docs.title: 2. Decision (report/rank_decision.json, rank_decision.csv)
docs.text:
Reference = CV column; target orientation/angle at e = 1.00; protected magnitude/delta and shape/shape at e = 1.00; anchor bound 0.05 + 2·sqrt(0.05·0.95/100) = 0.094; gain and loss multipliers 2.0.

Rank angle rate (SE) (a) gain: diff vs CV, threshold (b) anchor (c) protected: shape loss, threshold Qualifies CV 0.85 (0.036) reference — — — 3 0.86 (0.035) +0.01 ≤ 0.100 ✗ pass 0.00 ≤ 0.000 ✓ no 4 0.79 (0.041) −0.06 ≤ 0.108 ✗ pass 0.05 > 0.044 ✗ no 6 0.80 (0.040) −0.05 ≤ 0.107 ✗ pass 0.43 > 0.099 ✗ no 9 0.81 (0.039) −0.04 ≤ 0.106 ✗ pass 0.42 > 0.099 ✗ no 12 0.81 (0.039) −0.04 ≤ 0.106 ✗ pass 0.42 > 0.099 ✗ no

Magnitude/delta loss is 0.00 at every rank (power 1.00 everywhere). The anchor criterion passes at every rank (§5). Verdict keep_cv; the rationale string in the JSON lists the failing criteria per rank.

docs.title: 3. Rate versus rank, per mode (design_point_operating.csv, e = 1.00 rows; figure rank_ladder.png)
docs.text:
Mode / statistic CV 3 4 6 9 12 orientation / angle (target) 0.85 0.86 0.79 0.80 0.81 0.81 orientation / delta 0.91 0.93 0.84 0.53 0.47 0.47 orientation / shape 0.99 0.99 0.99 0.78 0.60 0.62 magnitude / delta (protected) 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 magnitude / angle 0.24 0.24 0.23 0.59 0.80 0.81 magnitude / shape 0.74 0.77 0.75 0.41 0.53 0.50 shape / shape (protected) 1.00 1.00 0.95 0.57 0.58 0.58 shape / angle 0.79 0.80 0.68 0.95 0.95 0.95 shape / delta 0.89 0.89 0.78 0.53 0.53 0.53 translation / delta · angle · shape 0.05 · 0.02 · 0.04 0.06 · 0.02 · 0.04 0.02 · 0.04 · 0.01 0.01 · 0.03 · 0.01 0.01 · 0.03 · 0.01 0.01 · 0.03 · 0.01

MC SE is ≤ 0.05 for every entry (0 where the rate is 0 or 1). component_selection is cv in the CV column and forced in every other column, with median_selected_lv equal to the forced rank (min_selected_lv = max_selected_lv = rank).

Does orientation angle power move with rank at n = 1200? No. It is 0.85–0.86 at CV and rank 3 and 0.79–0.81 at every rank from 4 to 12; the differences are within one pooled SE. Across effects (design_point_operating.csv, orientation/angle): CV 0.89 / 0.89 / 0.85 at e = 0.25 / 0.50 / 1.00; rank 4 0.75 / 0.76 / 0.79; ranks 6–12 0.86–0.87 / 0.81–0.83 / 0.80–0.81. The stage-supervised rank retains everything the angle test can use at this design point; components beyond n_stages − 1 add nothing to the target.

What a higher rank costs. Above rank 3 the latent space admits directions the stage label does not organize. shape power falls in every mode that has it — orientation 0.99 → 0.60–0.78, shape 1.00 → 0.57, magnitude 0.74 → 0.41–0.53 — and delta falls in the orientation and shape modes (0.91 → 0.47, 0.89 → 0.53). Only magnitude/delta is rank-invariant at 1.00. At the same time the off-target angle response rises: magnitude→angle 0.24 → 0.81 and shape→angle 0.79 → 0.95 by rank 9. A fixed rank above n_stages − 1 therefore degrades specificity in both directions: the geometry each mode targets is diluted, and PC1 of the stage configuration is rotated by group-specific noise directions the extra components carry.

Forced 3 versus CV. Every forced-3 entry is within 0.03 of the CV column (the largest difference is orientation/delta 0.93 vs 0.91). CV selection noise (range 2–3) is immaterial at this design point, so "fixed n_stages − 1" would be an operationally equivalent group-blind rule; it offers no gain, and CV remains the rule that adapts if the stage structure changes.

docs.title: 4. Covariates: eigengap and angle null width (design_point_operating.csv)
docs.text:
Row CV 3 4 6 9 12 anchor (none, e = 0) median eigengap 0.048 0.048 0.047 0.047 0.047 0.047 median angle null q95 (°) 5.9 6.0 10.8 10.9 11.1 11.2 IQR angle null q95 (°) 4.9 4.9 5.1 5.2 5.1 5.1 orientation e = 1.00 median eigengap 0.045 0.045 0.040 0.040 0.040 0.040 median angle null q95 (°) 11.5 10.2 17.0 15.6 16.2 16.4 IQR angle null q95 (°) 14.5 10.8 30.2 22.3 22.2 23.7

The recorded pooled eigengap is nearly constant across rank on identical data (0.048 → 0.047 at the anchor, 0.045 → 0.040 under orientation), the sanity check design D8 asked for: the ladder changes the measurement space, not the baseline geometry, and the small drop reflects the extra near-zero eigenvalues a larger configuration carries. The angle null, by contrast, widens as soon as rank exceeds n_stages − 1: the anchor's median q95 nearly doubles (5.9° → 10.8°) and the orientation column's dispersion doubles (IQR 14.5° → 30.2° at rank 4). A wider, more variable null with an unchanged eigengap is the signature of the extra components adding noise directions rather than signal, consistent with the pivotality finding that the null tracks the replicate's own latent configuration.

docs.title: 5. Anchors and Type I error
docs.text:
Per-column zero-effect anchors (design_point_operating.csv, none at e = 0, 100 replicates each):

Statistic CV 3 4 6 9 12 Bound delta 0.01 0.01 0.00 0.00 0.00 0.00 0.094 angle 0.02 0.02 0.02 0.02 0.02 0.02 0.094 shape 0.03 0.03 0.00 0.00 0.00 0.00 0.094

No rank inflates any anchor. At ranks ≥ 4 delta and shape reject 0 of 100 — a fixed rank above n_stages − 1 makes those tests conservative under the null, which the one-sided anchor bound does not penalize but which is one more cost of over-retention.

Independent-seed Type I controls at the baseline (type_i_table.csv, acceptance_report.csv, CV rank): none 0.06 / 0.05 / 0.07 (delta / angle / shape, combined 0.14); translation at e = 1.00 0.08 / 0.07 / 0.09 (combined 0.17). Every type_i_control target is met within 2 SE (acceptance_report.json).

docs.title: 6. Re-measurement at the chosen design point under CV (design_point_operating.csv, CV column)
docs.text:
The design-point pilot ran only orientation and translation; p_dmp had changed from 0.2 to 0.1. The CV column re-measures the other modes at the committed configuration:

Mode / statistic e = 0.25 0.50 1.00 magnitude / delta 1.00 1.00 1.00 shape / shape 0.95 0.97 1.00 orientation / angle 0.89 0.89 0.85 orientation / shape (cross-talk) 1.00 1.00 0.99 translation / angle 0.02 0.02 0.02

Magnitude and shape hold power ≥ 0.95 at every effect with p_dmp = 0.1. Orientation angle is flat across effects (0.85–0.89; differences within MC error).

Agreement with the design-point pilot. The pilot's ρ = 0, n = 1200 column gave orientation/angle 0.88 (SE 0.032) at e = 1.00 with median selected rank 3 and median eigengap 0.049 (results/phase5-design-point-2026-09-08/report/design_point_operating.csv); the ladder's CV column gives 0.85 (SE 0.036), rank 3, eigengap 0.045. The difference (0.03) is well within the pooled SE (0.048); the two runs draw different matched-seed families, so this is an independent replication of the design-point result.

Orientation → shape at the design point. At CV rank the projection-associated orientation→shape response is 0.99–1.00 at every effect — it does not decay at the committed rank. It decays only as the rank grows (0.99 → 0.78 → 0.60 → 0.62 at ranks 4 → 6 → 9 → 12 at e = 1.00; 0.98 → 0.96 at e = 0.25), as the 2026-09-03 probe found at the old design point, now confirmed on the corrected estimator at ρ = 0, n = 1200, p_dmp = 0.1. Since the rank is not being raised, Phase 5 keeps the item-2 predeclaration: orientation's shape response is reported as projection-associated cross-talk, not as evidence about the shape estimator.

docs.title: 7. Committed rule and limitations
docs.text:
Committed Phase 5 rank rule (group-blind): stage-supervised double cross-validation (plsda_doubleCV, modal LV across repeats with parsimony tie-break) selects the retained PLS rank; no group label enters the sizing. At the Phase 5 design point this yields rank 3 = n_stages − 1. The rule is committed for the design point Phase 5 runs; a fixed rank on real data would be a preregistered choice, not a tuned one, and this ladder gives no reason to make it.

Limitations:

  • One design point (ρ = 0, n = 1200, p_dmp = 0.1, four stages). The rank response could differ with more stages (where n_stages − 1 is larger) or a trending baseline (ρ = 0.8 moved the CV to rank 7–8 in the pilot).
  • 100 replicates: MC SE up to 0.05 per rate; the gain criterion could not detect an angle improvement smaller than ≈ 0.10. The observed differences are negative, so this does not change the verdict.
  • The rule's pooled SE treats paired columns as independent (conservative by design).
  • The anchor bound is one-sided (upper); the conservative delta/shape anchors at ranks ≥ 4 are reported, not penalized.
  • The eigengap is a property of the configuration in each column's latent space; its small drop with rank is a measurement-space effect, not a baseline-geometry change.
  • The code revision in PROVENANCE.txt is the pre-change commit plus the change's working tree (diff sha256 recorded); the merge commit of the change is the reproducible revision.

docs.title: Magnitude-construction diagnostic — 2026-09-10
docs.text:
Run: results/magnitude-construction-2026-09-10/ · Driver: scripts/magnitude_construction_diagnostic.py · Records read: results/phase5-2026-09-10/merged.jsonl (the paper-grade run, 9,500 units)

The paper-grade Phase 5 run returned gate decision HOLD on the two magnitude mandatory controls (magnitude/angle 0.276, magnitude/shape 0.742 against a 0.0695 bound). This diagnostic establishes what causes those responses and whether they are fixable, so the Phase 5 exit review can choose between a method revision and a claim revision on evidence.

Both verdicts point the same way: method revision. The magnitude surgery's off-target response is entirely an artefact of scaling one omic block's δ and not the others, and a construction that scales all three together is exactly size-pure in the measurement space. Nothing about the angle or shape estimators is implicated.

docs.title: 1. Mechanism: the response exists only in the concatenation
docs.text:
magnitude_kind='all' (semisynthetic.py) scales delta_methyl alone and leaves delta_expr and delta_protein at baseline, while the measurement space standardizes and concatenates all three omic blocks (evaluation.py). The per-omic scopes recorded in the paper-grade run show the consequence directly (block_decomposition.csv, checkpoint population_standardized, median over 500 replicates):

statistic scope e = 0.25 0.50 0.75 1.00 anchor angle methylation / expression / proteomics 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0 angle joint 6.6978 12.1199 16.5890 20.3293 0.0 shape methylation / expression / proteomics 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0 shape joint 0.0076 0.0138 0.0187 0.0226 0.0 delta methylation 9.9148 18.1365 24.8473 30.3300 0.0 delta expression / proteomics 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0

block_localization_summary.csv records the verdict as joint_only = True for magnitude/angle and magnitude/shape at population_standardized: every individual block is flat while the joint scope moves.

Within each omic block the surgery is exactly size-pure. The zeros are analytic, not small — angle is 0.0000 and shape lands at 8.4e-18, floating-point dust from the Procrustes routine. Only delta moves, and only in the block whose δ was scaled. The off-target response is created by concatenation: lengthen one component of a vector and leave the others, and the vector rotates. That is ordinary geometry, not a defect in any estimator.

Across all four checkpoints the causal chain is fully attributable:

checkpoint per-block angle joint angle population_native 0.0000 at every effect (no joint scope recorded) population_standardized 0.0000 at every effect 6.70 → 20.33 observed_standardized constant in effect (7.91 expression, 6.24 proteomics — a sampling floor) 10.70 → 21.96 pls_latent (joint only) 3.30 → 7.59

Two things follow that correct beliefs recorded in the repository:

  • It is not the methylation rev.logit nonlinearity. specificity.py previously stated that magnitude bends shape through that nonlinearity. At population_native — before any standardization and before any sampling — the per-omic angle and shape are 0.0000 at every effect, so the nonlinearity does not bend the methylation trajectory at all. The module docstring is corrected in this change.
  • The PLS projection attenuates the rotation rather than creating it. Joint angle is 20.33° at population_standardized and 7.59° at pls_latent. Whatever the latent space does here, it reduces the off-target geometry it is handed.

docs.title: 2. Constructibility: a size-pure magnitude change is realizable
docs.text:
The open question was whether scaling every omic's δ together survives per-block standardization, which z-scores each block on pooled data and so divides back out part of what the scaling adds. It does (uniform_delta_comparison.csv, population-standardized geometry, n_stages = 4):

construction e joint delta joint angle joint shape max block angle production (delta_methyl only) 0.25 5.9456 6.2898 1.095e-02 0.000e+00 production 1.00 18.1360 18.9097 3.288e-02 0.000e+00 uniform probe (all three δ) 0.25 14.9623 8.538e-07 9.558e-16 8.538e-07 uniform probe 1.00 44.7980 2.561e-06 9.995e-16 1.479e-06 anchor (e = 0, either) 0.00 0.0000 0.000e+00 1.008e-15 0.000e+00

The uniform-δ construction grows the trajectory strongly (joint delta 14.96 → 44.80) while holding joint angle at 8.5e-07 → 2.6e-06 and joint shape at ~1e-15 — the anchor's own floating-point floor — at every effect. Per-block standardization does not defeat it. A genuinely size-only magnitude change is constructible in this measurement space.

One calibration caveat for whoever adopts it: the effect axis is not comparable between constructions. At e = 1.00 the uniform probe reaches joint delta 44.80 against production's 18.14, because three blocks grow instead of one. A corrected mode needs its own effect-size calibration before its power curve can be read beside the existing one.

docs.title: 3. Shape-free confirmation
docs.text:
At two stages the trajectory is a single step and Procrustes shape is undefinable, so the orientation response can be observed with no possibility of shape contaminating it (uniform_delta_comparison.csv, n_stages = 2):

n_stages construction e joint delta joint angle joint shape 2 production 1.00 5.4250 19.0470 (undefinable) 2 uniform probe 1.00 12.9072 1.000e-06 (undefinable) 4 production 1.00 18.1360 18.9097 3.288e-02 4 uniform probe 1.00 44.7980 2.561e-06 9.995e-16

The production construction's joint angle is 19.05° at two stages against 18.91° at four — indistinguishable. The rotation is real and independent of the shape-removal step; it is not an artefact of Procrustes alignment in the four-stage design. This was a confirmation of an already-analytic finding and it confirmed it.

docs.title: 4. Localization: the instrument, recalibrated
docs.text:
localize_off_diagonal normalizes delta by mean path length and angle by 180°, but passes shape through raw. At e = 1.00 the joint values normalize to angle 20.3293/180 = 0.1129 (≥ the 0.05 cut → material) and shape 0.0226 (< 0.05 → not_material) — while the RRPP shape test rejects at 0.742. A single absolute cut cannot serve a statistic whose entire response range lies below it.

The recalibrated null_dispersion rule judges each excess in units of the zero-effect null's dispersion at the same checkpoint. Where that dispersion is degenerate — zero or dust, as it is at every population checkpoint for an analytically null construction (measured: delta sd exactly 0.0, angle sd 8.7e-07, shape sd 3.5e-16) — it falls back to "excess exceeds the dust tolerance", the limit of the rule as the null variance goes to zero. Each row records which path decided it.

Classifications under both rules (localization_by_rule.csv); 12 of 32 pairs change:

mode / statistic e absolute rule null-dispersion rule magnitude / angle 0.25–1.00 construction_present construction_present magnitude / shape 0.25–1.00 not_material construction_present orientation / delta 0.25–0.75 not_material construction_present orientation / delta 1.00 projection_associated construction_present orientation / shape 0.25 not_material construction_present orientation / shape 0.50–1.00 construction_present construction_present shape / angle 0.25–1.00 construction_present construction_present shape / delta 0.25–0.75 not_material construction_present shape / delta 1.00 construction_present construction_present translation / angle 0.25–1.00 not_material not_material translation / shape 0.25–1.00 not_material not_material

Two properties of that table matter more than the individual rows:

  • The negative control is preserved. Translation stays not_material on all eight rows under the recalibrated rule. The rule is calibrated, not merely permissive — its population off-target geometry is exactly zero, so nothing promotes it.
  • No response anywhere remains projection_associated. The paper-grade run's single such classification, orientation/delta at e = 1.00, becomes construction_present. Under the absolute rule its population-standardized excess fell below the 0.05 cut, so localization skipped forward to pls_latent; once the population checkpoint is judged against its own (degenerate) null, the response is seen where it actually first appears.

Interpretive shift this implies, stated plainly. Because population checkpoints carry analytically zero nulls, the recalibrated rule makes them very sensitive: any non-dust population-level off-target geometry now localizes as construction_present. That is the right standard for a localization instrument — a construction with any real off-target population geometry is impure, by definition, and the old cut was hiding real impurity behind an arbitrary threshold. But it answers "is this construction exactly pure?", not "is the impurity large enough to matter". The latter is read from the response magnitude, which the same tables carry. The exit review should not read construction_present as a severity claim.

docs.title: 5. What this hands the exit review
docs.text:
deviation from the paper-grade run what this diagnostic establishes revision implied mandatory_control[magnitude,angle] 0.276 Block-asymmetric δ scaling; exactly size-pure within every block; rotation confirmed shape-free at two stages; a uniform-δ construction is exactly pure in the joint space Method revision. Correct the magnitude construction to scale all omics' δ together, recalibrate its effect axis, and re-measure. The angle estimator is not implicated. mandatory_control[magnitude,shape] 0.742 Same mechanism; and the response was real all along — the 0.05 absolute materiality cut mis-reported it as not_material Method revision, same fix. The diagnostic prerequisite the paper-grade report named is discharged: the threshold is recalibrated and the pair now classifies. orientation/shape predeclared "projection-associated" Not supported. Orientation's response is present within each omic block (max block angle 90.08° against joint 89.93°; max block shape 0.108 against joint 0.059), and under the recalibrated rule no pair in the study is projection_associated Claim revision. Drop the projection-associated framing for orientation; it is construction-present cross-talk of a per-omic feature permutation. No gate impact — both orientation off-diagonals are descriptive roles. power[orientation,angle] monotonicity Untouched by this diagnostic — it is a property of the angle null's pivotality, not of a construction Claim revision, as the paper-grade report stated. Out of scope here.

Nothing here adopts a revision. The uniform-δ construction is reachable only from the diagnostic entry point (generate_semisynthetic_trajectory(..., _probe_uniform_delta=True)); it is not a magnitude_kind value, and a study configuration naming it is refused at load time. Adopting it as the production magnitude mode is the exit review's decision.

docs.title: 6. Reproduction
docs.text:
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/nix/store/61a1nwx3w6rqyaisj5rn1sal1981apm7-zlib-1.3.2/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
python scripts/magnitude_construction_diagnostic.py \
    --merged results/phase5-2026-09-10/merged.jsonl \
    --out-dir results/magnitude-construction-2026-09-10

Steps 1 and 2 read committed records only. Step 3 generates data but computes analytic population geometry — no sampling, no RRPP, no PLS fit — so the whole diagnostic runs on a workstation in minutes with no cluster and no R runtime. The LD_LIBRARY_PATH export is the local numpy/zlib workaround, not a project requirement.

docs.title: M-value/PLS trajectory specificity pilot
docs.text: Run date: 2026-07-29 to 2026-07-30 Code revision: 7cffff1 (main) Configuration: examples/trajectory_power_study/pilot_50x199.json

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This pilot tested the production PLS trajectory pipeline after correcting methylation integration to convert B values back to M values before standardisation and latent-space construction. The primary question was whether the previously observed magnitude-to-orientation cross-talk remained after that correction.

This is a medium-sized diagnostic run, not the paper-grade study. It used 50 replicates per cell, so a rejection rate near 0.05 has a Monte Carlo standard error of approximately 0.03.

docs.title: Primary result
docs.text:
The M-value correction removed the targeted magnitude cross-talk. At the largest magnitude effect, the intended delta test had complete power, while the angle and shape rejection rates remained below the nominal 0.05 level.

Injected mode Delta Angle Shape Magnitude 1.00 0.02 0.02 Orientation 0.72 0.76 1.00 Shape 1.00 0.84 1.00 Translation 0.02 0.04 0.08

Values are rejection rates at effect size 1.00, with 50 replicates per entry. Bold entries are the statistic intended to detect that mode. Translation is a negative control.

Magnitude specificity was stable across the entire effect-size sweep:

Effect size Delta Angle Shape 0.00 0.04 0.02 0.08 0.25 1.00 0.02 0.02 0.50 1.00 0.00 0.02 0.75 1.00 0.00 0.00 1.00 1.00 0.02 0.02

docs.title: Type I error and controls
docs.text:
The ordinary null cell was consistent with the nominal 0.05 level:

Baseline Delta Angle Shape Combined rule No difference 0.04 0.02 0.06 0.10 Translation control 0.06 0.02 0.10 0.14

All preregistered per-statistic Type I checks passed their two-Monte-Carlo-standard-error tolerance. The combined rule is descriptive here and was not among those individual Type I acceptance checks.

docs.title: Acceptance results
docs.text:
• Passed: all six Type I checks for the ordinary and translation baselines.
  • Passed: magnitude/delta power and monotonicity; top-effect power was 1.00.
  • Passed: shape/shape power and monotonicity; top-effect power was 1.00.
  • Failed: orientation/angle power target and monotonicity; rates across increasing effects were 0.00, 0.60, 0.66, 0.56, and 0.76.
  • Passed: all translation specificity checks and both magnitude off-diagonal checks.
  • Failed: orientation-to-delta, orientation-to-shape, shape-to-delta, and shape-to-angle specificity checks.

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text:
The pilot supports the rung-ladder conclusion that magnitude-to-angle leakage was caused by input representation rather than the trajectory estimator. Converting methylation to M-value space before PLS integration restores the expected separation: magnitude strongly affects delta without elevating angle or shape rejection.

The study does not establish general specificity of all three statistics. Orientation and shape injections still move multiple statistics. Those failures may reflect the definitions of the feature-space manipulations rather than a defect in the estimators: a global feature permutation can alter Procrustes shape as well as orientation, and relocating stage-specific feature support can change step lengths and angles as well as shape. This requires a separate geometry audit before interpreting those cells as estimator cross-talk.

The orientation curve is also non-monotone and misses the preregistered 0.80 top-effect power threshold (observed 0.76). With only 50 replicates, the standard error at 0.76 is approximately 0.06, but the strong off-diagonal rejection rates are too large to attribute to Monte Carlo noise.

docs.title: Decision and next work
docs.text: The targeted magnitude finding is strong enough to retain M-value conversion as the production contract. Before launching the 500-replicate paper-grade grid, audit orientation and shape injections in the pre-integration generative frame and verify that each is a pure change in its intended geometric quantity. Then repeat this pilot with corrected manipulations. Running the full study now would make the remaining cross-talk estimates more precise without resolving their interpretation.

docs.title: Net-displacement power comparison — 2026-10-14
docs.text:
Paper-grade power comparison of the net-displacement orientation estimator against PC1 in the production measurement space (openspec/changes/net-displacement-power-comparison/). It follows the net-displacement Type I study, whose verdict (paper_grade_power_comparison) selected it. It changes no production default; it names the change that would. Every rate below is read from results/net-displacement-power-2026-10-14/{phase6,phase5}/report/ (column_decision.csv/.json, design_point_operating.csv, eigengap_stratified_power.csv, acceptance_report.csv), …/{phase6,phase5}/consistency_checks.json and results/net-displacement-power-2026-10-14/comparison_decision.json, except where a number is marked as computed from merged.jsonl (§9 gives the snippet). Rates are rejection rates at p < 0.05 over 500 replicates × 999 permutations (Monte Carlo SE about 0.0097 at 0.05).

Runs: results/net-displacement-power-2026-10-14/phase6/ (SLURM array 920303) and …/phase5/ (array 920304) on ing · Code: db5ab69 (run and reports), 1ccded5 (consistency checks) · Column decisions: candidate_qualifies at both designs · Comparison: adopt_net_displacement.

In one paragraph. On identical datasets and permutation draws, replacing PC1 with the net-displacement orientation estimator in the cross-validated stage-PLS space raises orientation/angle power at the construction maximum from 0.300 to 0.648 at the Phase 6 small-n design and from 0.840 to 0.924 at Phase 5. It also clears every mandatory control at the one-sided bound 0.0695, which PC1 does not: PC1's angle rejects the shape construction at 0.138 (Phase 6) and 0.796 (Phase 5); net displacement rejects it at 0.054 and 0.022. Anchor size holds (0.050 at both designs). delta and shape are identical record for record between the two columns, as they must be. The predeclared rule therefore selects adopt_net_displacement, and the follow-up is the production-default flip. Two qualifications carry into the case study (§7): at n = 80 the gain is concentrated at the construction maximum and, within it, in replicates where CV retains more than three components (0.996 there, 0.280 otherwise), so a non-rejection stays uninformative; and the Phase 6 translation control sits one rejection under the bound (0.068).

docs.title: 1. Design
docs.text:
• Columns: two explicit design points (design_grid.points) on matched datasets:
column integration_method orientation_estimator role pls_cv × pc1 pls (CV rank) pc1 (null) baseline pls_cv × nd pls (CV rank) net_displacement candidate

No concat, pca, forced-rank or pls_within_group column; the probe's ceiling numbers are cited, not re-run. - Designs: - Phase 6 (examples/trajectory_power_study/net_displacement_power_phase6.json): three stages, group_stage_sizes = [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]], methylation + expression, base seed 800, family phase6-small-n. - Phase 5 (net_displacement_power_phase5.json): n = 1200, four stages, group_ratio 0.5, all three blocks, base seed 600, family phase5-primary. - Both use p_dmp = 0.1, ρ = 0, joint magnitude and surgery_censoring = error. - Cells (36 per design, 18,000 units): per column, the shared zero-effect anchor and four modes (magnitude, orientation, shape, translation) at e ∈ {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}, plus the engine's two type_i_baseline cells (independently seeded, measured in the baseline column). That is 1,000 Type I units and 8,500 units per column. - Seeds: both columns evaluate the same dataset at each replicate index. evaluation.seed is the constant 3 and is also the RRPP seed, so both columns draw the same permutation indices and the baseline column re-computes the parent studies' records (§6). - Rule: acceptance.column_decision (rule version 1), candidate pls × net_displacement against the baseline: - target orientation/angle at the top effect (1.0): Phase 6 criterion gain (candidate − baseline > 2 pooled SE); Phase 5 criterion no_loss (baseline − candidate ≤ 2 pooled SE), because PC1 is already near its ceiling there; - anchor delta/angle/shape ≤ α + 2·√(α(1 − α)/R) = 0.0695 at R = 500; - mandatory controls translation/angle, magnitude/angle, shape/angle at the top effect, each ≤ 0.0695; judged on the candidate only; - protected magnitude/delta, shape/shape: no loss beyond 2 pooled SE.

The cross-design selection (scripts/net_displacement_power_follow_up.py) returns adopt_net_displacement iff the candidate qualifies at both designs. Both rules are advisory: they change no default.

docs.title: 3. The rule's criteria
docs.text:
From column_decision.json / .csv. Bound 0.0695 everywhere (R = 500, no failed replicate).

criterion pair Phase 6 PC1 Phase 6 nd Phase 5 PC1 Phase 5 nd target orientation/angle, e = 1.0 0.300 0.648 0.840 0.924 anchor delta / angle / shape 0.026 / 0.024 / 0.020 0.026 / 0.050 / 0.020 0.036 / 0.046 / 0.048 0.036 / 0.050 / 0.048 control translation/angle, e = 1.0 0.028 0.068 0.042 0.040 control magnitude/angle, e = 1.0 0.008 0.030 0.024 0.000 control shape/angle, e = 1.0 0.138 0.054 0.796 0.022 protected magnitude/delta, e = 1.0 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 protected shape/shape, e = 1.0 0.228 0.228 0.996 0.996
  • Phase 6, gain: candidate − baseline = +0.348 against a threshold of 2 × pooled SE = 0.059. Passed.
  • Phase 5, no_loss: baseline − candidate = −0.084 against 0.040. Passed (it is a gain of 0.084, just over 4 pooled SE, but the rule asked only for no loss).
  • Anchor, controls, protected: passed at both designs. The baseline's shape/angle rates (bold) exceed the bound at both designs; the rule judges only the candidate, and the table shows both, as the design required.
  • Protected pairs carry no evidence here. Between two pls_cv columns, delta and shape are the same records' statistics (§6), so the protected criterion passes with loss exactly 0 by construction. It is declared for the rule's generality, not as a finding.
  • Translation control at Phase 6: 0.068 against 0.0695, one rejection under the bound, as in the Type I study (0.068). It is the narrowest margin in the comparison (§7).

Net displacement narrows the angle null and removes most of its across-replicate dispersion, the PC1 sign/flip tail. Two consequences for power:

Eigengap no longer gates power. Orientation/angle power within eigengap terciles at e = 1.0 (eigengap_stratified_power.csv):

design tercile eigengap range PC1 net displacement Phase 6 low 0.013–0.127 0.114 (0.025) 0.731 (0.034) Phase 6 middle 0.127–0.213 0.449 (0.038) 0.784 (0.032) Phase 6 high 0.213–0.441 0.337 (0.037) 0.428 (0.038) Phase 5 low 0.002–0.038 0.754 (0.033) 0.946 (0.017) Phase 5 middle 0.038–0.064 0.886 (0.025) 0.922 (0.021) Phase 5 high 0.064–0.181 0.880 (0.025) 0.904 (0.023)

PC1's low-tercile collapse (Phase 6 0.114; the Phase 6 report's "the cohort's own eigengap carries an orientation statement") is gone: net displacement does not need a well-determined principal axis. At e ≤ 0.75 its Phase 6 terciles are flat (0.08–0.21).

Rank still gates power at the Phase 6 maximum. Computed from merged.jsonl (integration_metadata.selected_lv): at Phase 6 orientation e = 1.0, 257 of 500 replicates retain more than three components (as in the parent study).

selected rank replicates PC1 net displacement ≤ 3 243 0.082 0.280 > 3 257 0.506 0.996

At e ≤ 0.75 every replicate retains at most three components and power is 0.084–0.178. The estimator raises power in both rank strata. The headline 0.648 is the mixture, and it depends on how often CV retains the group-specific variation the maximal construction creates, which the Phase 6 report found a six-donor change moves from 51 % to 8 %. At Phase 5 the rank is 2–4 throughout and power does not depend on it.

docs.title: 5. Acceptance targets (baseline column, descriptive)
docs.text:
From acceptance_report.csv. The profiles declare upper-bound Type I and specificity targets on the baseline column; the gate is off and the column rule does not read them.

  • Phase 6: all eleven targets met.
  • Phase 5: ten of eleven met. translation/shape in the type_i_baseline cell is 0.070 against 0.0695 (one rejection over), failing both type_i_control and specificity[translation, shape]. That cell is independently seeded, measured in the baseline column, and shape does not depend on the orientation estimator. The Type I study's Phase 5 type_i_baseline translation cell recorded the same rate (0.036 / 0.056 / 0.070), and the matched-seed translation cells here are 0.030–0.046 on shape at every effect. It is a Monte Carlo excursion at the bound in a statistic this comparison does not touch, not an estimator effect.

docs.title: 6. Consistency checks
docs.text:
From consistency_checks.json (scripts/net_displacement_power_checks.py, checks version 2).

(a) delta and shape are identical between the two columns. The estimator enters only _estimate_orientation, so the two columns' delta and shape cannot differ. Over 8,500 paired records per design (17,000 comparisons): 0 p-value mismatches at both designs. Observed statistics are bit-identical in 11,668 (Phase 6) and 9,221 (Phase 5) comparisons and differ in the rest by at most 9.0 × 10⁻¹¹ and 5.4 × 10⁻¹⁰ relative: BLAS rounding across separate processes, inside the checks' 1 × 10⁻⁹ tolerance and never enough to move a p-value.

(b) The baseline column reproduces the parent studies. It shares their generator seeds, evaluation parameters and RRPP seed, so wherever a parent record of the same mode, effect and replicate exists, its seed and p-values must be equal.

design parent records compared seed / p-value mismatches observed bit-identical max rel. diff. Phase 6 phase6-small-n-2026-10-09 6,500 0 / 0 5,285 3.1 × 10⁻⁸ Phase 6 phase6-small-n-magnitude-2026-10-09 2,000 0 / 0 1,167 3.1 × 10⁻⁸ Phase 5 phase5-2026-09-10 6,500 0 / 0 2,981 4.7 × 10⁻¹⁰ Phase 5 phase5-magnitude-2026-10-08 1,500 0 / 0 897 5.1 × 10⁻¹¹

8,000 of 8,500 (Phase 6) and 7,500 of 8,500 (Phase 5) baseline records have a parent. The uncovered cells are the new ones the design names: Phase 6 magnitude 0.75; Phase 5 magnitude 0.5 and 0.75. The 2,000 magnitude records of phase5-2026-09-10 are excluded from the comparison: that run generated magnitude under magnitude_kind: all, so its magnitude datasets differ despite equal seeds. The joint-construction parent phase5-magnitude-2026-10-08 covers magnitude 0.25 and 1.0.

The PC1 column's numbers are therefore the parent studies' recorded rates (e.g. Phase 6 orientation/angle 0.300, Phase 6 shape/angle 0.138), and the two columns are paired measurements of the same 500 datasets per cell.

Checks history. The first pass (checks version 1, db5ab69) exited 1 on both designs for two reasons, both in the checks rather than the records: (a) required bit-identical observed statistics and flagged the rounding above; (b) compared the Phase 5 joint-magnitude cells against the magnitude_kind: all parent (4,000 spurious p-value mismatches, all in magnitude). 1ccded5 adds the 1 × 10⁻⁹ tolerance and pairs parent records only within one magnitude construction (truth_metadata.transform.magnitude_kind); no record changed.

docs.title: 7. Decision and interpretability
docs.text:
comparison_decision.json (rule version 1; inputs phase6/report/column_decision.json sha256 c980fafb…, phase5/report/column_decision.json sha256 bdc3135e…):

  • Phase 6 candidate_qualifies (gain); Phase 5 candidate_qualifies (no_loss);
  • verdict adopt_net_displacement.

The verdict selects the follow-up change: flip SimulationEvaluationParams.orientation_estimator's production default to net_displacement in a separate change that re-pins the committed signatures, as default-joint-magnitude-construction did. Until that change lands, the default and every committed result stay PC1.

What angle means changes. Under net displacement, angle is the angle between the two groups' net displacement vectors (last stage mean − first stage mean) in the latent space, not between their principal axes. It reads only the endpoint stages. The paper and the case study must describe it that way.

Revised angle statement for the SEA-AD cohort (n = 80, ≥30 nuclei, RNA + ATAC), replacing the angle row of the Phase 6 report §8 once the default flips:

statistic rejection may be reported as evidence? non-rejection may be reported as evidence? angle Yes, that the groups' net directions of change differ. Type I is controlled (anchor 0.050; Type I study 0.048–0.058 in every space). Unlike PC1, the size, shape and location constructions do not move it: 0.024–0.068 at every effect, all within the bound, against PC1's up to 0.138 under shape. The translation construction sits at 0.058–0.068, near the bound, so a rejection alongside a location difference warrants care. The cohort's eigengap no longer conditions the statement. No. Power is 0.084–0.178 at e ≤ 0.75. At the construction maximum it is 0.648 overall, but 0.280 when CV retains three or fewer components (243 of 500 replicates) and 0.996 above that. Report the cohort's selected rank beside any angle result. A non-rejection is uninformative at n = 80.

At the Phase 5 design (n = 1200) angle has power 0.92–0.95 at every effect and is specific: shape → angle falls from 0.80 to 0.02. The orientation construction is still detected by shape (0.998–1.000) and delta (0.80–0.91) at Phase 5, and at Phase 6 by shape (0.464) and delta (0.354) at e = 1.0. Those are properties of the construction and of the other two statistics, which this change does not touch. The delta and shape rows of the Phase 6 statement are unchanged.

The rank-stratified and paired-outcome numbers (§2, §4) come from merged.jsonl:

from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from motco.simulations.grid import read_replicate_results
from motco.simulations.study.spectrum import record_design_point

def angle_frame(merged):
    rows = []
    for r in read_replicate_results(Path(merged)):
        if r.phase == "type_i_baseline":
            continue
        rows.append({
            "est": (record_design_point(r) or {}).get("evaluation.orientation_estimator") or "pc1",
            "mode": r.cell_metadata["trajectory_mode"], "e": r.cell_metadata["effect_size"],
            "rep": r.replicate_index, "rej": r.p_values["angle"] < 0.05,
            "lv": r.integration_metadata["selected_lv"],
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

d = angle_frame("results/net-displacement-power-2026-10-14/phase6/merged.jsonl")
o = d[(d["mode"] == "orientation") & (d.e == 1.0)]
print(o.assign(high=o.lv > 3).groupby(["high", "est"]).rej.agg(["mean", "size"]))      # §4 rank table
print(pd.crosstab(*o.pivot(index="rep", columns="est", values="rej").T.values))      # §2 paired counts

docs.title: Net-displacement Type I study — 2026-10-13
docs.text:
Paper-grade, null-only re-measurement of the net-displacement orientation estimator (openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-13-net-displacement-type-i-study/). It settles the Type I question that the orientation measurement probe left open. It runs no power cell, makes no power claim, and changes no production default. Every rate below is read from results/net-displacement-type-i-2026-10-13/{phase6,phase5}/report/ (anchor_decision.csv/.json, design_point_operating.csv, type_i_table.csv, acceptance_report.csv) and results/net-displacement-type-i-2026-10-13/follow_up_decision.json. Rates are rejection rates at p < 0.05 over 500 replicates × 999 permutations (Monte Carlo SE about 0.0097 at 0.05).

Runs: results/net-displacement-type-i-2026-10-13/phase6/ (SLURM array 917290) and …/phase5/ (array 917291) on ing · Code: 9089729 · Anchor decision: size_holds at every column at both designs · Follow-up: paper_grade_power_comparison.

In one paragraph. The probe found the net-displacement anchor angle rate at 0.08–0.10 in every space at both designs, against 0.01–0.05 under PC1, over 100 replicates. At 500 replicates × 999 permutations that excess does not reproduce. Every net-displacement column holds the predeclared bound 0.05 + 2·√(0.05·0.95/500) = 0.0695 on delta, angle and shape, at both designs. The lead arm, pls_cv × net_displacement, has anchor angle 0.050 at Phase 6 and 0.050 at Phase 5. Net displacement does move the anchor angle rate from conservative toward nominal at Phase 6 (PC1 0.024, net displacement 0.048–0.058); it is a size change within the bound, not an excess. The predeclared rule therefore selects the paper-grade power comparison of pls_cv × net_displacement against pls_cv × pc1. One caveat carries forward: under net displacement the translation control's angle rate sits near or above the anchor bound in some columns (Phase 6 concat 0.078), so the comparison should hold that control to the same bound (§5).

docs.title: Orientation measurement probe — 2026-10-12
docs.text:
Exploratory, matched-seed probe (openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-12-orientation-measurement-probe/). It ranks measurement arms for a paper-grade follow-up. It certifies none of them and changes no production default. Every rate below is read from results/orientation-measurement-probe-2026-10-12/ (rate_table.csv, checkpoint_table.csv, advancement_decision.json, summary.md). The motivating evidence in §1 is read from evidence/phase6_checkpoint_evidence.md, produced by scripts/orientation_checkpoint_evidence.py. Rates are rejection rates at p < 0.05 over 100 replicates (Monte Carlo SE about 0.022 at 0.05 and 0.05 at 0.5).

Run: results/orientation-measurement-probe-2026-10-12/ · Driver: scripts/orientation_measurement_probe.py at 49134c3 · Decision: no arm advances (advancement_decision.json, advisory).

In one paragraph. Two levers were crossed on the same datasets: the measurement space (five spaces) and the orientation estimator (PC1 or net displacement). The estimator turned out to be the larger lever. In the production stage-PLS space, net displacement more than doubles orientation/angle power at the Phase 6 SEA-AD design (0.29 → 0.67). At Phase 5 it removes the shape construction's leak into angle (0.89 → 0.02), and it costs no other power or specificity. That arm fails the predeclared rule on one criterion only: its Phase 6 anchor angle rate is 0.100, against a bound of 0.0936. Every net-displacement arm shows a similar anchor excess at both designs (0.08–0.10, against 0.01–0.05 under PC1). At 100 replicates this is suggestive, not established, and it is the question the follow-up must settle first. The alternative spaces do not help on their own terms: - pls_within_group without a per-permutation refit is invalid (anchor angle up to 0.88). - pca and pls_forced at rank 2(K − 1) recover the rotation, but they lose Phase 6 shape power (0.19 → 0.00–0.01) and leak angle into the shape or magnitude cells.

docs.title: 1. Motivating evidence
docs.text:
From evidence/phase6_checkpoint_evidence.md (Phase 6 small-n orientation profile, baseline column, results/phase6-small-n-2026-10-09/merged.jsonl, sha256 6a91a47e…):

e population (native methylation) observed std. PLS latent, rank ≤ 3 PLS latent, rank > 3 angle rate (≤ 3 / > 3) 0.25 41.4° 58.3° 21.6° — 0.034 / — 0.50 60.0° 71.5° 24.8° — 0.058 / — 0.75 75.7° 81.8° 28.5° — 0.090 / — 1.00 90.0° 89.8° 32.1° (n = 243) 76.0° (n = 257) 0.082 / 0.506

The signed anchor angle has a heavy tail: q95 = 137.1° in the observed space and 135.6° in the latent space. On that oracle threshold the signed observed angle separates e = 1 from the anchor in 0.000 of replicates, and its folded counterpart in 0.996 (0.496 in the latent space).

docs.title: 2. Design and provenance
docs.text:
• Arms: five spaces × two estimators, giving ten arms:
  • Spaces: pls_cv (production stage-PLS, CV rank; with PC1 this is the reference arm); pls_forced (stage-PLS at rank 2(K − 1)); pls_within_group (K − 1 components per group, fixed basis, no refit inside RRPP); pca (rank 2(K − 1)); and concat (ceiling reference, never eligible).
  • Estimators: pc1 and net_displacement.
  • Designs:
  • Phase 6 SEA-AD: three stages, group_stage_sizes = [[11, 10, 28], [9, 10, 12]], methylation + expression measured.
  • Phase 5: n = 1200, four stages, all three blocks measured.
  • Both use p_dmp = 0.1, ρ = 0, joint magnitude and surgery_censoring = error.
  • Deviation: the Phase 5 design uses the joint magnitude construction, not the methylation-only all pinned in phase5_power_study.json. The reference arm's rates are recomputed here, and every comparison is against them.
  • Cells: the anchor; orientation at e = 0.5 and 1.0; magnitude and shape at e = 1.0. Each cell has 100 replicates × 199 permutations.
  • Seeds: the generator seed is matched across cells per (design, replicate). One RRPP seed per unit is shared by all ten arms, so arms differ only in measurement.
  • Run: SLURM array 912606 on ing, 50 shards. 1,000/1,000 units and 10,000 arm records, with 0 failures. It took 28.2 recorded core-hours, 28 % over the 22 core-hour budget written before launch (PROVENANCE.txt).

docs.text:
From checkpoint_table.csv: median realized angle at orientation e = 1.0, and the median retained rank.

arm Phase 6 latent Phase 6 rank Phase 5 latent Phase 5 rank pls_cv__pc1 63.9° 4 72.0° 3 pls_cv__net_displacement 56.7° 4 6.1° 3 pls_forced__pc1 71.1° 4 89.5° 6 pca__pc1 90.5° 4 90.2° 6 pls_within_group__pc1 90.3° 4 90.2° 6

The population angle is 90.0° and the observed standardized angle is 89.7–90.3° in every arm.

  • Label-free and two-sided spaces keep the full rotation. pca and pls_within_group reproduce the observed angle. The CV stage-PLS space shrinks it.
  • Phase 5 under net displacement. The pls_cv latent angle is only 6.1°, yet the test still rejects in 0.89 of replicates, because its anchor median is 0.3°.
